a629.speaker: Gen. Abraham Manyuat, Inspector General of Police (South Sudan)
a629.name: Gen. Abraham Manyuat
a629.title: Inspector General of Police (South Sudan)
a629.speech: Said one of his key priorities while in office is transforming the police force into a professional and decent law enforcement; outlined that police officers must operate effectively, respond promptly to incidents, and utilize available resources to maintain law and order, and stressed that police officers should enhance their legal understanding to ensure they apply laws correctly and uphold justice in their duties: “Our priorities will focus on three or four things, one of which is qualifying the police in terms of efficiency, endurance, ethics, and behaviour” ; “They should have knowledge of the laws, which is in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law, and we will continue training them in various fields, and filtering out those who are not in good health from the service.”

a629.speaker: Gen. Abraham Manyuat, Inspector General of Police (South Sudan)
a629.name: Gen. Abraham Manyuat
a629.title: Inspector General of Police (South Sudan)
a629.speech: Said he plans to promote ethical conduct, discipline, and respect for human rights within the police force to foster public trust and improve community relations, and stated that his administration will ensure that police officers are equipped with the necessary work tools: “We will work to ensure that they have the work equipment to do their job well, but above all, we will focus on the values and ethics of police work, and that they respect human rights.” ; “They should not be part of corruption and are not corrupt, and they should also be helpful to women and children and elderly people, and this is the work that we will focus on.”

a637.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization (post on X)
a637.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a637.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization (post on X)
a637.speech: Said that the situation at Kamal Adwan Hospital in the northern Gaza Strip is “truly horrific” amid the continuing bombardment by the Israeli occupation ; said the WHO and its partners had reached the hospital two days earlier, amid Israeli attacks and bombardment, and had delivered 5,000 litres of fuel as well as quantities of food and medicine, and explained that the organization had transferred three patients from Kamal Adwan Hospital to Al-Shifa Hospital so that their treatment could continue ; stated that clashes and Israeli bombardment were continuing near the hospital, causing further damage to the oxygen supply and the electricity generators.

a637.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization
a637.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a637.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization
a637.speech: Noted that Israel had last week arbitrarily refused to allow WHO staff to enter Kamal Adwan Hospital, and that these events had deprived the hospital of staff specialised in surgery and obstetric care.

a637.speaker: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Director-General of the World Health Organization
a637.name: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus
a637.title: Director-General of the World Health Organization
a637.speech: Renewed his call for a ceasefire in Gaza, for health services to be protected, and for the hellish atmosphere to be brought to an end.

a713.speaker: Country Strategy Paper (CSP) 2025-2030 consultations report
a713.name: Country Strategy Paper (CSP) 2025-2030 consultations report
a713.speech: According to the consultations, for decades Eswatini has grappled with a key impediment to its growth, the slow progress towards higher-value production; the consultations underscored that this challenge has persisted far too long and that the time for change is now. "Stakeholders overwhelmingly endorsed this approach, recognizing that the key to long-term prosperity lies in moving away from outdated systems and embracing a more diversified and innovative economic model," states the report. ; "The coming years will be crucial in shaping Eswatini's economic future. With the right investments, collaboration, and commitment, the Kingdom has the chance to turn its economic challenges into opportunities for sustainable growth, inclusive development," reads the report.

a713.speaker: CSP mission team
a713.name: CSP mission team
a713.speech: Proposed an aggressive strategy to tackle this economic bottleneck, accelerating structural transformation - pushing beyond traditional economic models and pursuing strategies that diversify the economy, enhance resilience and build competitiveness.

a713.speaker: Stakeholders at the consultations (government ministries, private sector leaders and development partners)
a713.name: Stakeholders at the consultations (government ministries
a713.title: private sector leaders and development partners)
a713.speech: Agreed on the need to focus on two strategic priority areas - investing in climate-resilient infrastructure and strengthening competitiveness - and agreed that boosting private sector development from entrepreneurship to large-scale industry must be a priority; there was a strong consensus that achieving these goals requires enhanced coordination between government, development partners and the private sector and more effective aid coordination.

a713.speaker: Government of Eswatini
a713.name: Government of Eswatini
a713.speech: Expressed strong support for the CSP and commended the work of the Bank in facilitating successful consultations; recognized the milestone achievements in driving the country's socio-economic development and highlighted the importance of continued collaboration between stakeholders; sees the establishment of the Liaison Office as essential for strengthening the relationship between Eswatini and international partners and, as Eswatini's portfolio grows, called for a bolstered presence at this office to ensure smoother communication and more impactful outcomes.

a755.speaker: Millennium Development Authority (MiDA) (announcement)
a755.name: Millennium Development Authority (MiDA) (announcement)
a755.speech: Announced Alex Mould as its new Chief Executive Officer, following the departure of Michael Asare Bediako.

a755.speaker: Michael Asare Bediako, outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
a755.name: Michael Asare Bediako
a755.title: outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
a755.speech: As he stepped down, expressed gratitude for the support he received, stating his confidence in MiDA's continued success under its new leadership.

a755.speaker: Michael Asare Bediako, outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
a755.name: Michael Asare Bediako
a755.title: outgoing Chief Executive Officer of MiDA
a755.speech: Has assured a smooth transition, having already engaged Mr Mould in discussions to ensure the continuity of strategic initiatives, and remains optimistic about MiDA's future and its impact on Ghana's development.

a804.speaker: Insecurity Insight (report)
a804.name: Insecurity Insight (report)
a804.speech: According to a new report by Insecurity Insight, the suspension of USAID funding by President Donald Trump has intensified negative perceptions of international aid in the Sahel region; the report, which analyzed online discussions in Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger, reveals a surge in negative sentiment towards NGOs and international donors following President Trump's January 20th, 2025 executive order freezing USAID funding, sentiment often intertwined with nationalist and pro-Russian rhetoric; the report highlights a rise in pro-Russian narratives, portraying Russia as a more reliable and respectful partner compared to the West.

a804.speaker: Insecurity Insight (report)
a804.name: Insecurity Insight (report)
a804.speech: Warns that the suppression of pro-aid voices online is contributing to a shrinking humanitarian space; the report highlights the unintended consequences of the USAID funding freeze, emphasizing the need for careful consideration of the potential impact of aid policies on local perceptions and the humanitarian space.

a804.speaker: Online users in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger (cited in the report)
a804.name: Online users in Burkina Faso
a804.title: Mali and Niger (cited in the report)
a804.speech: Online discussions show a significant increase in criticisms of international aid, with many users expressing concerns about economic dependency, corruption, and perceived Western interference; some users view the USAID funding freeze as a sign of declining Western commitment to the region.

a996.speaker: Somali media groups and civil society groups
a996.name: Somali media groups and civil society groups
a996.speech: Have vehemently denounced new efforts by the Somali Ministry of Information to impose restrictions on independent reporting.

a996.speaker: A media representative who withdrew from the meeting (anonymous)
a996.name: A media representative who withdrew from the meeting (anonymous)
a996.speech: "We were invited to the meeting, but we decided to leave after the Deputy Minister of Information, Abdirahman Al-Adaala, began threatening journalists and media leaders. That is not acceptable. This man has been known to have committed many crimes against journalists."

a996.speaker: A participant representing a private NGO (anonymous)
a996.name: A participant representing a private NGO (anonymous)
a996.speech: "Shortly after the opening remarks, we were supposed to join a panel, but the whole thing became dramatic after all journalists and representatives of the independent media left in anger. The Deputy Minister of Information began harassing journalists with his speech, which included threats against private media."

a996.speaker: Religious leaders attending the meeting
a996.name: Religious leaders attending the meeting
a996.speech: Proposed a hardline Islamist version of censorship under the guise of countering "immoral and indecent content."

a996.speaker: Yusuf Hussein Jimale (Madaale), Mayor of Mogadishu
a996.name: Yusuf Hussein Jimale (Madaale)
a996.title: Mayor of Mogadishu
a996.speech: Falsely claimed that social media had "facilitated the spread of homosexuality" and called for severe punishment, and stated that his office had recruited new police specifically to combat "immorality": "The Banadir Regional Administration has created its own police force to protect morals. We have seen boys pretending to be girls and girls pretending to be boys on social media. This homosexuality is something we cannot accept."

a996.speaker: Daud Aweys, Minister of Information
a996.name: Daud Aweys
a996.title: Minister of Information
a996.speech: Announced plans to propose new guidelines for controlling social media, claiming it had become a means to incite and spread disinformation against the government.

a996.speaker: Ali Abdirahman, invitee who did not attend
a996.name: Ali Abdirahman
a996.title: invitee who did not attend
a996.speech: Expressed his frustration with the recent crackdown on social media influencers and independent journalists: "The meeting's agenda was to send a stern warning that the government is going to crush dissenting voices under the guise of 'incitement and disinformation,' while disinformation often comes from the government itself. I chose not to attend such a gathering."

a996.speaker: Abdalle Mumin, SJS Secretary General
a996.name: Abdalle Mumin
a996.title: SJS Secretary General
a996.speech: "We have already said that this is going to be worse. We condemn the new tactics intended to censor independent and critical media reporting. We support and praise the unity of independent media and their journalists and stand by them to ensure that media freedom and freedom of expression are not violated in the country."

a996.speaker: Hashi Nur, media expert
a996.name: Hashi Nur
a996.title: media expert
a996.speech: Called for the government to focus on more pressing issues rather than curtailing freedom of expression: "The government needs to focus on important issues. We are struggling with insecurity, massive corruption, and rampant sexual violence against women and girls. The same government officials are committing these crimes, but sadly they are wasting their time trying to curtail the public's right to freedom of expression."

a1282.speaker: European Union
a1282.name: European Union
a1282.speech: has announced an initial humanitarian assistance budget of €1.9 billion for 2025 to address growing global crises, of which €510 million has been earmarked for Nigeria and other countries in sub-Saharan Africa.

a1282.speaker: European Union delegation to the Federal Republic of Nigeria and ECOWAS (statement)
a1282.name: European Union delegation to the Federal Republic of Nigeria and ECOWAS (statement)
a1282.speech: "With more than 300 million people needing humanitarian assistance in 2025, the EU is upholding its commitment to help those most in need as a leading donor of humanitarian assistance. Our humanitarian aid funding will support our partners on the ground – the UN family, the Red Cross/Red Crescent family, international and local government and non-governmental organisations – to provide life-saving, emergency assistance where needed." ; According to the statement, the fund will be distributed to West and Central Africa, the Sahel, the Lake Chad Basin, North-West Nigeria, Central Africa, the Great Lakes region, and the Greater Horn of Africa.

a1282.speaker: European Union (statement on regional allocations)
a1282.name: European Union (statement on regional allocations)
a1282.speech: The EU said, "The region has seen significant changes in recent months, including after the recent developments in Syria." ; The EU has also allocated another €470 million to target vulnerable populations in the Middle East and North Africa, mainly Gaza and Yemen; €95 million to North Africa and Yemen; €140 million to Ukraine; €8 million to Moldova; "an initial €113 million will be directed at addressing the domestic and regional impact of the crisis in Venezuela, the needs of the most vulnerable people affected by the armed conflicts in Colombia, the complex crisis in Haiti and the violence in Central America, Mexico and Ecuador." ; "Around €182 million in Asia will be allocated to humanitarian assistance, particularly for the Myanmar crisis and its impact in Bangladesh, as well as for the situation in Afghanistan. Moreover, €35 million are allocated to the Southern Africa and Indian Ocean region as well as €5 million in the southern Caucasus and Central Asia." ; "More than €295 million are reserved for worldwide actions, responding to sudden-onset emergencies and unforeseen humanitarian crises that may arise throughout the year. Over €110 million will be committed to horizontal activities, including innovative projects and policy initiatives, for example, the multi-year programmatic partnerships and the enhanced response capacity."

a1394.speaker: Foreign ministry associated with the Sudanese army
a1394.name: Foreign ministry associated with the Sudanese army
a1394.speech: Has proposed a strategy for conducting elections, including establishing a transitional government, appointing a civilian prime minister, and facilitating a national dialogue with civil society.

a1394.speaker: Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan, Sudan's military leader
a1394.name: Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan
a1394.title: Sudan's military leader
a1394.speech: Mentioned that Sudan has proposed a potential "roadmap" that includes a "constitutional transition" and the possibility of free elections in the future. He noted that a national dialogue would involve all significant factions and conflicting parties within the country.

a1394.speaker: Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan, Sudan's military leader (on Gaza)
a1394.name: Gen. Abdel-Fattah Burhan
a1394.title: Sudan's military leader (on Gaza)
a1394.speech: Expressed his strong backing for Arab leaders' reconstruction initiatives for Gaza during a summit in Cairo on Tuesday and reiterated Sudan's "steadfast support for the Palestinian people" in their pursuit of an independent state in line with the two-state solution: "We firmly oppose any initiatives that seek to displace our Palestinian brothers from their homeland under any guise, as this poses a threat to Arab national security and to regional and global stability."

a1394.speaker: Arab leaders (at the Cairo summit)
a1394.name: Arab leaders (at the Cairo summit)
a1394.speech: Endorsed Egypt's post-war strategy for the Gaza Strip, which aims to allow the approximately 2 million Palestinians to remain, countering U.S. President Donald Trump's proposal to depopulate the area; their approval of the $53 billion plan was a clear rejection of Trump's vision.

a1394.speaker: Hamas
a1394.name: Hamas
a1394.speech: Praised the outcomes of the summit.

a1394.speaker: Israel
a1394.name: Israel
a1394.speech: Dismissed the outcomes of the summit.

a1394.speaker: Trump administration
a1394.name: Trump administration
a1394.speech: Met the outcomes of the summit with a tepid reaction.

a1706.speaker: Degodia (Dagoodiye) community of Mogadishu's Xamar Jajab district
a1706.name: Degodia (Dagoodiye) community of Mogadishu's Xamar Jajab district
a1706.speech: Has issued a strongly worded appeal to international ambassadors, alleging ongoing human rights violations, land grabbing, and systemic marginalization targeting their community.

a1706.speaker: Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a1706.name: Secretariat of the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD)
a1706.speech: Extends its appreciation to the Parliament of the Republic of Kenya following its formal approval of the IGAD Treaty.

a1706.speaker: Equality Now
a1706.name: Equality Now
a1706.speech: Is urging the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights to call upon African Union (AU) member states to urgently address rising sexual violence and exploitation of women and girls across the continent.

a1706.speaker: Somali intelligence sources (anonymous)
a1706.name: Somali intelligence sources (anonymous)
a1706.speech: Told Horn Observer that Somalia is preparing to send a high-level delegation to Iraq this weekend amid growing concerns over a secret security agreement that could signal Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) expansion into East Africa.

a1706.speaker: Multiple sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1706.name: Multiple sources familiar with the matter (anonymous)
a1706.speech: Said secret negotiations have been ongoing since early May between Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud and senior Al-Shabaab figures from the Hawiye clan.

a1706.speaker: Kenyan police
a1706.name: Kenyan police
a1706.speech: Are describing the shooting dead of Kenyan Member of Parliament Hon. Charles Ong'ondo Were on Wednesday evening in Nairobi as a targeted and premeditated attack.

a1781.speaker: Ken Ndala, Secretary for Education (Malawi)
a1781.name: Ken Ndala
a1781.title: Secretary for Education (Malawi)
a1781.speech: Said that processes analysing the costs and where the resources will come from were underway ; said when developing such initiatives, there has to be an analysis in terms of where the resources would come from ; sounded optimistic that the policy will start in January 2026 and that he did not anticipate immediate donor support ; “In the first place, the Ministry of Education itself has two ministries [Basic and Secondary and High Education], this on its own is a cost. These are the issues that as technocrats we want to analyse and make some savings and then say why can’t we refocus these resources towards free secondary education? We also need to restrict the way we spend our resources like on travels and not just at the Ministry of Education, but the whole system. Further, government has an obligation to increase resources towards the sector.”

a1781.speaker: Ken Ndala, Secretary for Education (Malawi)
a1781.name: Ken Ndala
a1781.title: Secretary for Education (Malawi)
a1781.speech: Said the ministry was banking on government providing funding, not donors: “The donors are going to come, but as government we have to show commitment that we want to carry out this as a reform. We have tentative figures, but we are still doing an upscale analysis in terms of what is actually needed for government to have this in place. The key word is prioritising resources. We are also working with Treasury on how we are going to get resources.”

a1781.speaker: The Nation (newspaper analysis)
a1781.name: The Nation (newspaper analysis)
a1781.speech: Established last week that the 12-year free-cycle of education, covering examination fees, identity cards and school development fund (SDF) at both primary and secondary levels would cost K412 billion each year.

a1781.speaker: United Nations Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) (analysis of the 2025/26 education budget)
a1781.name: United Nations Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) (analysis of the 2025/26 education budget)
a1781.speech: Has expressed fears that the 50 percent reduction in US Agency for International Development (USAid) funding from 2024 to 2025 risks reversing hard-won gains in Malawi’s education sector ; argued that the creation of the Ministry of Higher Education, with an allocation of seven percent of the sector’s budget, resulted in a redistribution of resources as the share managed by the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education declined from 39 percent in 2024/25 to 27 percent in 2025/26 fiscal year.

a1781.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, Civil Society Education Coalition executive director
a1781.name: Benedicto Kondowe
a1781.title: Civil Society Education Coalition executive director
a1781.speech: Said the proposed modalities raise feasibility concerns: “A sustainable approach requires a clear cost roadmap that secures predictable domestic financing—possibly through the national budget framework—while progressively engaging development partners for targeted support.”

a1781.speaker: Alipo Kaphwiyo, Catholic University of Malawi head of the Education Department
a1781.name: Alipo Kaphwiyo
a1781.title: Catholic University of Malawi head of the Education Department
a1781.speech: Said experience from the 1994 Free Primary Education shows that the goal was quantity over quality because adequate resources were not provided ; “Government has to ensure that adequate and relevant physical, material and human resources are made available in all public schools before implementation of the policy, strategies for sustainability must be put in place.”

a1781.speaker: Willy Kambwandira, accountability expert
a1781.name: Willy Kambwandira
a1781.title: accountability expert
a1781.speech: Has said promises on cutting travel are normally met with lack of enforcement and administrative sanctions on senior government officers who defy such directives.

a1786.speaker: Modibo Mao Makalou, economist and financial manager, former collaborator of President Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT) from 2002 to 2012
a1786.name: Modibo Mao Makalou
a1786.title: economist and financial manager, former collaborator of President Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT) from 2002 to 2012
a1786.speech: Paid tribute to ATT: "My memories are inexhaustible under ATT's tenure, which was a fabulous adventure carried out in the company of a heterogeneous but remarkable team led by an exceptional leader to raise Mali to the firmament of African countries" ; "Head of State, humanitarian, international mediator and then President of the Republic, his love for the homeland was boundless, he had a visceral interest in everything that concerned his country and his fellow citizens and never lost sight of the general interest" ; described him as affable, polyglot, humanist, endowed with a great sense of humour, simple, humble and courteous, a mark of great souls ; said posterity will remember that he had acquired his renown throughout the world for having kept his word by masterfully leading a turbulent transition in order to hand power to a democratically elected regime ; said that for his part he lost an elder brother for whom he had great admiration and above all a mentor.

a1786.speaker: Modibo Mao Makalou, economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.name: Modibo Mao Makalou
a1786.title: economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.speech: Assessed ATT's record: said that from 2002 to 2012 ATT's record was globally positive, even laudable, highlighting the construction of tens of thousands of social housing units, the quadrupling of the electricity access rate in Mali (from 8% to 32%), the financing of drinking water at the Kabala plant for 170 billion CFA francs, the obtaining in 2006 of a grant from the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) by the government of the United States of America in the amount of 460.8 million US dollars, i.e. 244.8 billion CFA francs, to reduce poverty and increase economic growth over 5 years, the construction of thousands of kilometres of roads and rural tracks to open up the interior and exterior, and the drafting and implementation of an agricultural orientation law to modernise the primary sector and ensure food and nutrition security.

a1786.speaker: Modibo Mao Makalou, economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.name: Modibo Mao Makalou
a1786.title: economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.speech: Said ATT's programme during his first term from 2002 to 2007 was set out in sixteen points summarised in five major priority areas: the restoration of the moral authority and effectiveness of the State; the consolidation of a united, just, participatory society open to the world; rural development; the development of a competitive, modern, job-creating economy; and the anchoring of Mali in its history, culture and value system ; said ATT had results-based management, was an immense worker, and had bet heavily on youth, intending to hand over the baton to the next generation.

a1786.speaker: Modibo Mao Makalou, economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.name: Modibo Mao Makalou
a1786.title: economist and former collaborator of ATT
a1786.speech: Said that unfortunately geopolitics and geostrategy cut short ATT's plans with the destabilisation of Mali and of the Sahelo-Saharan region through conflicts, terrorism and insecurity, and currently the devastating effects of inflation and climate change on people's living conditions ; said ATT was a fierce advocate of African integration, had a very dynamic diplomacy based first on good neighbourliness, and believed socio-economic and productive investments would improve his fellow citizens' standard of living ; said ATT preferred a consensual approach to the management of public affairs, around the theme "Let us find again what unites us", because in his view it is union that makes strength and division that weakens nations.

a1786.speaker: Amadou Koïta, former member of the Mouvement citoyen and former minister
a1786.name: Amadou Koïta
a1786.title: former member of the Mouvement citoyen and former minister
a1786.speech: "Mali needs a leader like ATT, a man of peace, dialogue, consensus and duty" ; "ATT was the champion of development, he was devoted to the cause of Mali" ; "I ask the current leaders and the current political class to take ownership of the legacy of President Amadou Toumani Touré. He was first and foremost a man of peace and dialogue, of consensus, of duty. For ATT, to govern is to serve but not to serve oneself. For ATT, to govern is to fight every day for the interest of the country, it is to bring Malians together, to unite Malians around the essential, it is to ensure that all Malian women and all Malian men take part in the work of unifying a new Mali."

a1786.speaker: Amadou Koïta, former member of the Mouvement citoyen and former minister
a1786.name: Amadou Koïta
a1786.title: former member of the Mouvement citoyen and former minister
a1786.speech: Paid tribute to ATT's record: said ATT was the soldier who, after taking power on 26 March 1991, committed to organising a successful transition and peacefully handing power to the democratically elected president, organising one of the most successful transitions in Africa ; said that on the political level ATT was a man of consensus who from his accession to power in 2002 advocated consensual management, bringing rival political parties (the PSP, the RDA, the democratic movement parties and the MPR) around the cabinet table ; said that on the economic level there were structural reforms that allowed the Malian economy to become an emerging economy, citing thousands of kilometres of roads, the 3rd Bridge of Bamako, the interchange of the 2nd bridge, the Wabaria bridge in Gao, the University of Kabala, the Hospital of Mali, the Somino Dolo hospital in Sévaré, the development of thousands of hectares, the Farmers' Day, the Women's House, free caesarean sections, compulsory health insurance (AMO), the Millennium Challenge, five kilometres of roads in every regional capital, youth employment through the creation of the APEJ, and social housing ; said the Millennium Challenge made it possible to develop thousands upon thousands of hectares at the Office du Niger and to renovate Bamako airport, as well as the construction of the Kadhafi canal at the Office du Niger.

a1786.speaker: Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT), former President of Mali, as quoted by Amadou Koïta
a1786.name: Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT)
a1786.title: former President of Mali, as quoted by Amadou Koïta
a1786.speech: "that the development of a country passes first through the development of roads".

a1786.speaker: Thierno Oumar Hass Diallo, former minister
a1786.name: Thierno Oumar Hass Diallo
a1786.title: former minister
a1786.speech: "I carry ATT in my heart ..." ; "Simplicity of the soldier, love of the homeland, ATT will have been a fine example of a statesman ..." ; said that to speak of ATT stirs emotion in him, and that he could hardly speak of the man without Lobbo, his wife, and Seydou Sissouma, a symbol of loyalty in collaboration ; recalled ATT's physical presence every year at the Week of the Albino Child which he initiated on behalf of the SOS Albinos Association, noting that the first time ATT was on site at the Islamic Centre of Hamdallaye before the organisers ; said ATT was a republican who never uttered the name of the sitting Head of State in their conversations, always saying "the President" ; "Simplicity of the soldier, love of the homeland, of positive spirit, ATT will have been a fine example of a statesman full of humility. Rest in peace, Child of Mopti!"

a1786.speaker: Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT), former President of Mali, as quoted by Thierno Oumar Hass Diallo
a1786.name: Amadou Toumani Touré (ATT)
a1786.title: former President of Mali, as quoted by Thierno Oumar Hass Diallo
a1786.speech: "Thierno, from my hotel room in Bangui, I could hear the noise of the bombs. People do not know war. I do not wish it for Mali" ; "Thierno, are you leaving? Rest assured that wherever you are, I will keep a watchful eye on you."

a1821.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a1821.name: Bill Gates
a1821.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a1821.speech: Has urged African leaders to seize the moment to accelerate progress in health and development through innovation and partnership, despite current headwinds. He announced that the majority of his $200 billion spend over the next 20 years will go to Africa, with a focus on partnering with governments that prioritise the health and wellbeing of their people. "I recently made a commitment that my wealth will be given away over the next 20 years. The majority of that funding will be spent on helping you address challenges here in Africa." ; "By unleashing human potential through health and education, every country in Africa should be on a path to prosperity and that path is an exciting thing to be part of."

a1821.speaker: Bill Gates, Gates Foundation Chair
a1821.name: Bill Gates
a1821.title: Gates Foundation Chair
a1821.speech: Spoke about the transformative potential of artificial intelligence (AI), noting its relevance for the continent's future. He praised Africa's young innovators, saying he was "seeing young people in Africa embracing this and thinking about how it applies to the problems that they want to solve." Drawing a parallel to the continent's mobile banking revolution, he added, "Africa largely skipped traditional banking and now you have a chance, as you build your next generation healthcare systems, to think about how AI is built into that."

a1821.speaker: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, and Amina J. Mohammed, Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1821.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
a1821.title: Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, and Amina J. Mohammed, Deputy Secretary-General of the United Nations
a1821.speech: Echoed calls for collaboration and shared responsibility.

a1821.speaker: Graça Machel, advocate for women and children
a1821.name: Graça Machel
a1821.title: advocate for women and children
a1821.speech: Described the current situation as "a moment of crisis" and emphasised the importance of enduring partnerships in Africa's development journey. "Mr Gates' long-standing partnership with Africa reflects a deep understanding of these challenges and a respect for African leadership, ideas and innovation. We are counting on Mr Gates' steadfast commitment to continue walking this path of transformation alongside us."

a1821.speaker: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organisation
a1821.name: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala
a1821.title: Director-General of the World Trade Organisation
a1821.speech: Stressed that Africa's health progress is a result of strong government leadership, resilient communities and partnerships that deliver results.

a1842.speaker: Nato leaders (joint statement)
a1842.name: Nato leaders (joint statement)
a1842.speech: Said they were united against "profound security threats and challenges, in particular the long-term threat posed by Russia to Euro-Atlantic security and the persistent threat of terrorism" ; reaffirmed their "ironclad commitment to collective defence" - the Article Five mutual security guarantee if any one member comes under attack.

a1842.speaker: Mark Rutte, Nato Secretary General
a1842.name: Mark Rutte
a1842.title: Nato Secretary General
a1842.speech: "No-one should doubt our capacity or determination should our security be challenged. This is a stronger, fairer and more lethal alliance that our leaders have begun to build." ; Told Nato leaders that they were meeting at a "dangerous moment", and that the defence alliance's guarantee of mutual defence - "an attack on one is an attack on all, sends a powerful message".

a1842.speaker: Mark Rutte, Nato Secretary General
a1842.name: Mark Rutte
a1842.title: Nato Secretary General
a1842.speech: Said decisions made on Wednesday would include continued support for Ukraine while pushing for peace.

a1842.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1842.name: Donald Trump
a1842.title: US President
a1842.speech: Had earlier appeared to raise questions about the security guarantee, referring to "various definitions of Article Five", but said after the summit: "I stand with [Article Five], that's why I'm here."

a1842.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1842.name: Donald Trump
a1842.title: US President
a1842.speech: Hailed the summit as a "big success". He had said earlier that the hike in spending would be a "great victory for everybody, I think. We will be equalised shortly, and that's the way it has to be".

a1842.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1842.name: Donald Trump
a1842.title: US President
a1842.speech: "He's got a little difficulty, Zelensky, a nice guy. I've spoken to Putin a lot... he volunteered help on Iran. I said do me a favour, help us on Russia, not Iran."

a1842.speaker: Carlos Cuerpo, Spanish Economy Minister
a1842.name: Carlos Cuerpo
a1842.title: Spanish Economy Minister
a1842.speech: Said Madrid was making an "enormous effort" to reach a target of 2.1% and "the discussion about the percentage is misguided".

a1842.speaker: Pedro Sánchez, Spanish Prime Minister
a1842.name: Pedro Sánchez
a1842.title: Spanish Prime Minister
a1842.speech: Signed Nato's statement, maintaining that it was "sufficient, realistic and compatible" for Madrid to meet its commitments while paying less.

a1842.speaker: Bart de Wever, Belgian Prime Minister
a1842.name: Bart de Wever
a1842.title: Belgian Prime Minister
a1842.speech: Told reporters that while it wouldn't be easy "3.5% within 10 years is a realistic goal".

a1842.speaker: Peter Pellegrini, Slovak President
a1842.name: Peter Pellegrini
a1842.title: Slovak President
a1842.speech: Indicated that Bratislava would not stand in the way of the big hike in defence spending, about which Slovakia had raised concerns.

a1842.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a1842.name: Emmanuel Macron
a1842.title: French President
a1842.speech: Took issue with President Trump's trade tariff confrontation with the European Union and called for a deal: "We can't say to each other, among allies, we need to spend more... and wage trade war against one another, it makes no sense."

a1842.speaker: Nato member states (final communique)
a1842.name: Nato member states (final communique)
a1842.speech: Stressed their commitments to providing support for Ukraine, "whose security contributes to ours", adding that direct contributions to Kyiv's defence and its defence industry would be included in assessment of allies' defence spending.

a1842.speaker: Sir Keir Starmer, UK Prime Minister
a1842.name: Sir Keir Starmer
a1842.title: UK Prime Minister
a1842.speech: Said Nato was as relevant and important now as it had ever been: "We live in a very volatile world and today is about the unity of Nato, showing that strength. We're bigger than we were before, we're stronger than we were before."

a1978.speaker: Mohamud Moalim Abdulle, Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a1978.name: Mohamud Moalim Abdulle
a1978.title: Commissioner of the Somali Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA)
a1978.speech: Has lauded the decision by the Somali Council of Ministers to allocate $500,000 for humanitarian assistance in the Awdal region ; speaking on behalf of SoDMA, welcomed the initiative, underscoring its role in strengthening the country's capacity to respond to natural disasters ; noted that this financial contribution would facilitate the delivery of essential aid, including food, clean water, and medical supplies, to the most vulnerable families within the region.

a2038.speaker: Study published in World Development Perspectives
a2038.name: Study published in World Development Perspectives
a2038.speech: According to the study, Malawians prefer community-led initiatives over traditional top-down approaches often tied to foreign aid. The research, conducted in nine rural Malawian communities, found that community leaders possess the necessary knowledge and skills to spearhead development projects.

a2038.speaker: Frank Kasonga, Executive Director of Mudzi Connect and co-author of the study
a2038.name: Frank Kasonga
a2038.title: Executive Director of Mudzi Connect and co-author of the study
a2038.speech: Emphasized the importance of community participation in development projects: "Community-led development prioritizes the community's participation in contrast to external contractors or organizations at every level of a project."

a2038.speaker: A study participant (anonymous)
a2038.name: A study participant (anonymous)
a2038.speech: "Community ownership of development projects is key to sustainability of development as it brings a sense of responsibility to the community."

a2099.speaker: Bloomberg
a2099.name: Bloomberg
a2099.speech: Reported on Thursday that the American oil company Exxon Mobil will lay off approximately two thousand employees worldwide, around 4% of its workforce, as part of a "restructuring" plan.

a2099.speaker: Lusa (citing Bloomberg)
a2099.name: Lusa (citing Bloomberg)
a2099.speech: According to Lusa, which cites Bloomberg, Exxon's "restructuring" will mean laying off between 3% and 4% of its employees worldwide and is focused on cost reduction.

a2099.speaker: Conoco Phillips
a2099.name: Conoco Phillips
a2099.speech: Announced plans to lay off up to a quarter of its workforce, less than a month earlier.

a2109.speaker: Israeli government
a2109.name: Israeli government
a2109.speech: Has condemned France's recognition of the State of Palestine.

a2109.speaker: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli Prime Minister (post on his official X handle)
a2109.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
a2109.title: Israeli Prime Minister (post on his official X handle)
a2109.speech: "We strongly condemn President Macron's decision to recognise a Palestinian state next to Tel Aviv in the wake of the October 7 massacre. Such a move rewards terror and risks creating another Iranian proxy, just as Gaza became. A Palestinian state in these conditions would be a launch pad to annihilate Israel - not to live in peace beside it. Let's be clear: the Palestinians do not seek a state alongside Israel; they seek a state instead of Israel."

a2109.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President (post on his official X handle)
a2109.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2109.title: French President (post on his official X handle)
a2109.speech: Announced that France will formally recognise the State of Palestine, saying the decision aligns with France's "historic commitment to a just and lasting peace in the Middle East": "Consistent with its historic commitment to a just and lasting peace in the Middle East, I have decided that France will recognise the State of Palestine." ; added that the formal announcement will be made at the United Nations General Assembly in September: "I will make this solemn announcement before the United Nations General Assembly this coming September."

a2109.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, French President
a2109.name: Emmanuel Macron
a2109.title: French President
a2109.speech: Stressed the urgent need to end the war in Gaza, provide humanitarian assistance, and secure the region, calling for the demilitarization of Hamas and the rebuilding of Gaza: "The urgent priority today is to end the war in Gaza and to bring relief to the civilian population. We need an immediate ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and massive humanitarian aid for the people of Gaza. We must also ensure the demilitarization of Hamas, secure and rebuild Gaza." ; emphasised that the future Palestinian state must be committed to peace and coexistence, with full recognition of Israel.

a2109.speaker: SaharaReporters
a2109.name: SaharaReporters
a2109.speech: Earlier reported that, in a major diplomatic shift, French President Emmanuel Macron announced that France will formally recognise the State of Palestine, making it one of the most influential Western nations to take such a step amid the ongoing conflict between Israel and Hamas.

a2223.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.name: Kyeh Kim
a2223.title: Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.speech: "We would like to identify the main problems, the interventions, as well as carry out feasibility studies, so that we can implement right after the signing of the programme. Perhaps in April 2026," she told journalists during a joint press conference with the deputy prime minister.

a2223.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.name: Kyeh Kim
a2223.title: Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.speech: Acknowledged budget constraints, but guaranteed that they would do their best to fight for an adequate envelope to be able to deal with some of the needs of this programme.

a2223.speaker: Kyeh Kim, Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.name: Kyeh Kim
a2223.title: Vice-President of the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC)
a2223.speech: Highlighted the positive impacts of the partnership between the MCC and the government and stressed previous investments in infrastructure and development: "In recent years we have had an excellent partnership with the Government of Cabo Verde. These programmes have had a lasting impact on the people of Cabo Verde and on the national economy. We invested in the port of Praia, in streets and bridges, agriculture, private sector development and land administration" ; said the new phase of cooperation will focus on exploring the transport and digital economy sectors, to help connect Cabo Verde with itself and with the world.

a2223.speaker: Olavo Correia, Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2223.name: Olavo Correia
a2223.title: Deputy Prime Minister of Cabo Verde
a2223.speech: Praised the partnership with the MCC and recognised the relevance of the Regional Compact for the country's development: "It is an enormous privilege for us to once again receive the vice-president of the MCC. We have signed a fund of 6.3 million dollars to help prepare the project. This Compact will be transformative, helping Cabo Verde to connect better internally and with the world" ; "We want a digital, connected Cabo Verde with a strong economy, with employment and growth opportunities for our young people and women."

a2268.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (official statement)
a2268.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a2268.title: African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (official statement)
a2268.speech: Announced on Wednesday in an official communiqué that King Mohammed VI, in his capacity as Chairman of the Al-Quds Committee, had given his High Instructions for the immediate delivery of emergency humanitarian and medical aid to the Palestinian people, in particular the civilian populations of the Gaza Strip, facing a humanitarian crisis of exceptional gravity.

a2268.speaker: United Nations agencies
a2268.name: United Nations agencies
a2268.speech: Warn of the depletion of food stocks, the saturation of hospitals, permanent insecurity and the lack of vital resources; more than 80% of health infrastructure is said to be partially or totally out of service, while displaced populations are deprived of any lasting access to water, electricity or safe shelter.

a2275.speaker: Federal Accounts Allocation Committee (data)
a2275.name: Federal Accounts Allocation Committee (data)
a2275.speech: A SaharaReporters reporter's review of the Federal Accounts Allocation Committee data has shown that state and local governments received N96 billion as ecology funds between December 2023 and November 2024.

a2275.speaker: Nigerian Government
a2275.name: Nigerian Government
a2275.speech: Recently, the Nigerian Government warned of flooding in 30 states of the country and the FCT.

a2275.speaker: Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (published data)
a2275.name: Office of the Accountant General of the Federation (published data)
a2275.speech: According to data published by the Office of the Accountant General of the Federation, in November 2024, states received N4.607 billion, while local governments across the country received N3.839 billion as an ecology fund.

a2275.speaker: United Nations Children's Education Fund (UNICEF) (statement on its website)
a2275.name: United Nations Children's Education Fund (UNICEF) (statement on its website)
a2275.speech: In 2022, the United Nations Children's Education Fund noted that 2.5 million people in Nigeria needed humanitarian assistance due to flooding. Sixty per cent of these were children. ; "The floods, which have affected 34 out of the 36 states in the country, have displaced 1.3 million people. Over 600 people have lost their lives and over 200,000 houses have either been partially or fully damaged," a statement on UNICEF's website read.

a2275.speaker: Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP)
a2275.name: Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP)
a2275.speech: In 2022, the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) urged then President Muhammadu Buhari to "direct the Attorney General of the Federation and Minister of Justice Mr Abubakar Malami, SAN, and appropriate anti-corruption agencies to promptly and thoroughly investigate the spending of Ecological Fund by governments at all levels - federal, state and local governments from 2001 to 2022."

a2414.speaker: Peter Wiebler, USAID Mission Director
a2414.name: Peter Wiebler
a2414.title: USAID Mission Director
a2414.speech: Said Government's careful stewardship of the economy has been extremely challenging, but necessary to bring Zambia out of debt distress and on the path for long term sustainable growth; commended Government for not only the development of its current national budget, but on the overall careful management of the economy despite the many fiscal challenges, made harder by the drought and electricity crisis; recognised that developing a budget and maintaining fiscal discipline had been hard, especially during this time of drought and load shedding ; "Your careful stewardship of the economy has been extremely challenging but necessary to bring Zambia out of debt distress and on the path for long term sustainable growth. We are proud to partner with you in this work - through USAID's Revenue for Growth programme as well as our Good Financial Governance programme, which we co-fund with Germany and the European Union. We affirm our support to the reforms undertaken in partnership with the International Monetary Fund (IMF)."

a2414.speaker: Peter Wiebler, USAID Mission Director
a2414.name: Peter Wiebler
a2414.title: USAID Mission Director
a2414.speech: Pointed out that USAID supported Zambia providing K520 million in food and emergency assistance for food aid and drought response assistance; said this assistance was part of more than K1.7 billion the US government had pledged to Zambia to address the current drought and strengthen food security, among others.

a2414.speaker: Dingani Banda, Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) Commissioner-General
a2414.name: Dingani Banda
a2414.title: Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) Commissioner-General
a2414.speech: Said the contribution of tax revenue to the national budget had progressively increased over the recent years, from a share of 49 percent of the national budget in 2021 to 70.5 percent in 2024, a development he said was testament to the increasing reliance on domestic revenue for Government expenditure, away from borrowing and donor dependency ; "This year, ZRA is expected to collect K125.3 billion, compared to a target of k103.1 billion last year. Undoubtedly, the authority has an enormous task ahead, but we are confident that we will rise to the occasion and exceed the target. Strengthening collaboration with stakeholders such as the Zambia Association of Manufacturers, Zambia Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Zambia Chamber for Small and Medium Business Associations, is now our anchor of hope for success in 2024."

a2707.speaker: Dr Adili Kachima, Superintendent of Prisons and TB and HIV Coordinator at the Prisons Health and Nutrition Unit (PHNU)
a2707.name: Dr Adili Kachima
a2707.title: Superintendent of Prisons and TB and HIV Coordinator at the Prisons Health and Nutrition Unit (PHNU)
a2707.speech: Highlighted the project's impact during World AIDS Day in Songea, Ruvuma Region: "This project has significantly improved HIV and TB control measures, especially in managing TB cases within prisons. It has enhanced access to medical equipment, facilitated the recruitment of health workers and promoted self-awareness among beneficiaries."

a2707.speaker: Dr Eva Matiko, THPS Director of Programmes
a2707.name: Dr Eva Matiko
a2707.title: THPS Director of Programmes
a2707.speech: Shared key achievements from October 2023 to September 2024: the project provided HIV testing to 89,602 individuals, of whom 2,030 tested positive; 1,362 clients were diagnosed with TB and received appropriate treatment, while 2,697 individuals comprising people living with HIV and children under five exposed to TB successfully completed TB Preventive Therapy.

a2707.speaker: Dr Eva Matiko, THPS Director of Programmes
a2707.name: Dr Eva Matiko
a2707.title: THPS Director of Programmes
a2707.speech: Reaffirmed the project's commitment to supporting the government's efforts to expand access to HIV and TB prevention, care and treatment services by improving and strengthening healthcare systems to deliver high-quality, efficient care.

a2821.speaker: Dr Hilarious Abiwu, Acting Programme Manager, National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), Ghana
a2821.name: Dr Hilarious Abiwu
a2821.title: Acting Programme Manager, National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), Ghana
a2821.speech: Said malaria deaths had dropped by 97 per cent, from 2,137 in 2015 to just 74 in 2024 ; said parasite prevalence reduced from 27.5 per cent to 8.6 per cent over the last decade, while malaria's share of outpatient cases had fallen to 16 per cent, down from nearly half in past years ; said Ghana became the first country globally to introduce both the RTS,S and R21 vaccines, protecting millions of children.

a2821.speaker: Dr Hilarious Abiwu, Acting Programme Manager, National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), Ghana
a2821.name: Dr Hilarious Abiwu
a2821.title: Acting Programme Manager, National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP), Ghana
a2821.speech: Noted that despite these gains, progress remained fragile, highlighting critical challenges that posed a threat to Ghana's elimination agenda, including a $78 million funding gap, with Indoor Residual Spraying particularly affected, threats of drug and insecticide resistance, and over-reliance on external support, with cuts from some donors like USAID ; said the NMEP had called for renewed advocacy and partnership through government, the legislature (Parliament), the private sector and agencies, and that the programme is mobilising the UK's voice in the Global Fund replenishment and leveraging UK-Ghana commercial partnerships ; said on a broader strategy the programme was ensuring malaria elimination became an all-of-government, all sectors and a society-wide mission ; “Ghana, through progress achieved over the period, shows that elimination is possible. But elimination will only be achieved if we combine science, innovation, political leadership, and sustainable financing. Zero malaria is within reach only if we act together.”

a2821.speaker: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, Minister of Health of Ghana
a2821.name: Kwabena Mintah Akandoh
a2821.title: Minister of Health of Ghana
a2821.speech: Highlighted Ghana's ambitious commitment to elimination, marked by the launch of the National Malaria Elimination Strategic Plan (NMESP 2023-2028), and celebrated the country's pioneering role as the first in the world to deploy both the RTS,S and R21 malaria vaccines ; underscored Ghana's US$2 million pledge to the Global Fund, a historic milestone in Africa's domestic financing for malaria ; noted progress in parliamentary advocacy, citing the collaboration between the NMEP and the Parliamentary Select Committee on Health, which led to the establishment of the Malaria Caucus in Parliament and the successful push for funding to implement Indoor Residual Spraying in two regions ; reiterated Ghana's unwavering commitment to malaria elimination, noting that while the country was advancing toward greater self-reliance, sustained international support remained essential, especially in the face of tightening global funding ; “Ghana's journey from malaria control to elimination reflects true leadership and the strength of partnership, science, and political commitment. With continued domestic investment and international solidarity, zero malaria is within reach.”

a2902.speaker: United Nations (UN)
a2902.name: United Nations (UN)
a2902.speech: A few days before a tragic 2nd anniversary for Sudan, the UN launched a new appeal to the international community at a press conference held on Thursday in New York.

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: Described a situation without precedent in recent history: « Sudan is currently the only country in the world where famine is officially confirmed. » According to him, it is the third famine recorded since the start of the 21st century — a dramatic indicator of the seriousness of the crisis ; « All the indicators converge: this is the most serious humanitarian crisis at present », affirmed Shaun Hughes.

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: Mr Hughes, who has met many displaced families, testifies to their harrowing accounts: « Women told me how they fled the fighting with their children, travelling hundreds of kilometres in terrifying conditions. »

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: For the WFP, this catastrophe is avoidable. « It is a man-made crisis, fuelled by the conflict but also by deliberate obstacles to the delivery of aid », denounced Mr Hughes.

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: The WFP coordinator calls for unrestricted humanitarian access. « We are not asking for the impossible. We must be able to reach populations across front lines, borders and contested areas, without administrative blockages », he says.

a2902.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) agency
a2902.name: World Food Programme (WFP) agency
a2902.speech: The agency also demands to be able to reopen its offices, redeploy its teams, and obtain the visas and authorisations necessary to act effectively; to assist 7 million people within six months, the WFP needs an additional $650 million — 80% of its projected budget — plus $150 million to support refugees in Chad, South Sudan and the Central African Republic.

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: « Without funding, we have to reduce the number of beneficiaries or the quantities of aid. That is already the case: this month, rations were lowered to 70% in famine zones, and to 50% in at-risk ones », warned Mr Hughes.

a2902.speaker: Shaun Hughes, regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.name: Shaun Hughes
a2902.title: regional coordinator of the World Food Programme (WFP)
a2902.speech: « The Sudanese people need, above all, a ceasefire. It is time to put an end to hostilities, so that everyone can finally rebuild their lives », concluded the WFP representative.

a3043.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a3043.name: Salva Kiir
a3043.title: President of South Sudan
a3043.speech: has instructed the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security to supply tractors and farm equipment to farmers in a bid to enhance food security and promote large-scale local food production across the country ; emphasized the importance of empowering farmers to produce food locally, highlighting the need to shift away from reliance on food imports ; underscored that equipping farmers with the necessary tools would not only improve food availability but also contribute to national stability and economic growth.

a3043.speaker: Lily Albino Akol, Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a3043.name: Lily Albino Akol
a3043.title: Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security
a3043.speech: directed all state governors and chief administrators to allocate 250,000 hectares of land each for agricultural use.

a3043.speaker: Hussein Abdelbagi, Minister of Agriculture
a3043.name: Hussein Abdelbagi
a3043.title: Minister of Agriculture
a3043.speech: said 104 tractors received in April from the Ministry of Finance will be distributed to agricultural associations and cooperatives, and not to individuals ; said the move aims to strengthen organized farming and increase productivity across the country.

a3043.speaker: Farmers across South Sudan
a3043.name: Farmers across South Sudan
a3043.speech: have consistently raised concerns about conflicts, insufficient government support, particularly in pest control, access to fuel, and lack of a stable market for their produce.

a3047.speaker: Kassim Haroun Ali, Minister Delegate in charge of Decentralisation
a3047.name: Kassim Haroun Ali
a3047.title: Minister Delegate in charge of Decentralisation
a3047.speech: In his address, first thanked USAID for its financial support and for its concern to contribute to the development of the interior regions, which are considerably behind in the socio-economic field. He also recalled that this support fits perfectly with the objectives of the ministry, which has set local development through support to civil society among its priorities ; concluded his remarks on the precious nature of this support and suggested to Djiboutian civil society as well as to elected officials and representatives of the State that they derive maximum benefit from this programme in order to improve the living conditions of the populations living in the interior regions.

a3073.speaker: Umar Aliyu, witness
a3073.name: Umar Aliyu
a3073.title: witness
a3073.speech: Said the driver was coming from a quarry site at the nearby Arab road on high speed only to be interrupted by other commercial vehicles picking passengers at the bus stop; “In the process of negotiating, the truck fell into a drainage and it affected many people standing at the bus stop, who either wanted to cross or waiting for vehicles.’’

a3073.speaker: A nurse attending to the injured victims at Kubwa General Hospital
a3073.name: A nurse attending to the injured victims at Kubwa General Hospital
a3073.speech: Told our reporter that five people were rushed to the hospital, comprising two females and three males, adding that one of them is still unconscious.

a3073.speaker: Officials of the Federal Road Safety Commission
a3073.name: Officials of the Federal Road Safety Commission
a3073.speech: Declined to comment on the incident.

a3185.speaker: Tian Lin, Director General of the International Cooperation Department of the Chinese international cooperation agency
a3185.name: Tian Lin
a3185.title: Director General of the International Cooperation Department of the Chinese international cooperation agency
a3185.speech: Said the agency provides technical and financial assistance wherever the need is expressed, notably in developing countries: "China has 60 million poor people and works tirelessly to lift them out of this circle. Despite its own challenges, the country is willing to support developing countries" ; Indicated that to fight poverty effectively and secure the planet, the agency subscribes to the 2030 agenda for sustainable development, with 500 projects financed by China around the world.

a3185.speaker: Tian Lin, Director General of the International Cooperation Department of the Chinese international cooperation agency
a3185.name: Tian Lin
a3185.title: Director General of the International Cooperation Department of the Chinese international cooperation agency
a3185.speech: Specified that the agency operates on the principle of non-interference in the states where it intervenes: "China does not impose its vision on partner countries. The essential thing is to give priority to transparency in carrying out development projects in everyone's interest. We work for the connection of developing countries in order to build a world of peace and stability" ; Said that in its conception of foreign aid the agency draws inspiration from the principle of "teaching a man to fish rather than giving him a fish" - sharing know-how to help others qualitatively transform their daily lives.

a3327.speaker: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
a3327.name: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)
a3327.speech: Calls on the poorest countries to take a leading role in directing external loans and aid for their development; developing countries should take ownership of their development agenda and manage the allocation of external development finance in alignment with their national development priorities.

a3327.speaker: UNCTAD 2019 Least Developed Countries Report
a3327.name: UNCTAD 2019 Least Developed Countries Report
a3327.speech: As the report shows, LDCs account for around 20 of the most aid-dependent countries due to persistent shortfalls in their domestic savings and per capita income; the report indicates that Ethiopia is at high risk of paying back its debt with zero account capacity, that the resource gap remained about 15 percent of its GDP, and that Ethiopia has 52 billion in debt of which 26 billion is external debt covering 33 percent of GDP, with less than 10 percent of targeted aid reaching the targeted area.

a3327.speaker: World Bank and International Monetary Fund debt sustainability framework
a3327.name: World Bank and International Monetary Fund debt sustainability framework
a3327.speech: In May 2019, five countries were in debt distress, 13 in high risk of debt, 17 moderate risks and nine were in low risk of debt.

a3327.speaker: Committee for Development Policy (CDP), group of independent experts reporting to the UN Economic and Social Council
a3327.name: Committee for Development Policy (CDP)
a3327.title: group of independent experts reporting to the UN Economic and Social Council
a3327.speech: Reviews the LDC criteria every three years; according to per capita income, human asset and economic vulnerability, currently 47 countries have been designated as least developed countries of the world, 32 from Africa, eight Asian and seven from Oceania.

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Says of the country's "over-reliance on maize as a food and economic staple means poor harvests immediately trigger inflation volatility" ; quoted as saying "inflation remains one of Malawi's most stubborn economic challenges and that the highest in southern African region [and that] though it recently declined from 30% to just below 29%, the figure is still the highest in the Southern African region" ; said the drop "is temporary and directly linked to seasonal improvements in food availability, particularly maize — thus country's overreliance on maize as a food and economic staple means poor harvests immediately trigger inflation volatility"

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Reported that Malawi's GDP growth remains modest, projected at 3.2% in 2024, largely driven by a rain-fed, low-mechanisation agriculture sector: "This structural dependency on climate-sensitive agriculture renders the economy vulnerable to weather shocks. Historical events — including severe droughts, Cyclone Freddy, the CoVID-19 pandemic, and global conflicts such as the war in Ukraine — have repeatedly disrupted supply chains and impacted economic resilience."

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Warned that due to the way debt is accounted for — in Malawi Kwacha — any devaluation of the currency leads to a passive increase in the debt burden; highlighted that some of Malawi's debts date back to the 1970s and are still being serviced today; reiterated that while government does not default on its obligations, debt servicing costs significantly constrain government to effectively deliver the much-needed public services such as health, education and infrastructure.

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Identified key issues impacting Malawi's economic stability: limited forex sources; disinformation and social media speculation triggering inflationary expectations and panic economic behaviours; a widespread informal economy including black market forex trading; and diaspora remittance channels like hawala reducing formal inflows.

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Presented a broad reform strategy centred on production-led growth and homegrown economic models: diversifying agriculture through large-scale irrigation and mega farms (Nchalo, Karonga, Nkopola); mining sector growth including three recent mining agreements and a planned University of Mining; debt restructuring through bilateral negotiations; private sector engagement by commercial banks; and a tailored monetary framework developed by the RBM in the absence of an IMF programme.

a3445.speaker: Mafuta Mwale, Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.name: Mafuta Mwale
a3445.title: Governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi (RBM)
a3445.speech: Reported on the suspension of the Extended Credit Facility that "the programme was initially meant to stabilise the economy, but it became misaligned with evolving economic shocks"; that some assumptions such as automatic fuel price adjustments were unrealistic and donor support did not materialise as expected, and that the suspension is temporary and mutually agreed upon with the IMF; emphasised that Malawi must begin to take ownership of its economic policies, stating, "Let Malawians be their own IMF".

a3445.speaker: Public Affairs Committee (PAC) report on the 6th All-Inclusive Stakeholders Conference
a3445.name: Public Affairs Committee (PAC) report on the 6th All-Inclusive Stakeholders Conference
a3445.speech: Says Mafuta Mwale began by acknowledging the significance of the conference as a timely platform to engage citizens on economic issues, and that his presentation was structured around economic performance indicators, external sector developments, fiscal trends, the debt burden, and proposed solutions to Malawi's macroeconomic challenges; observes that the session "served as a sobering reflection of Malawi's economic situation, which is viewed as being at a cross-road", that "the presentations and debates reinforced the urgency of transitioning from dependency on foreign aid and weather-sensitive agriculture to a resilient, production-oriented economy", that "while the suspension of the ECF has created uncertainty, it also presents an opportunity for Malawi to redefine its economic trajectory", and that "the overarching call was clear — Malawi must craft and implement homegrown, inclusive, and sustainable economic strategies, driven by national unity, transparency, and citizen accountability".

a3445.speaker: Simplex Chithyola Banda, Minister of Finance of Malawi
a3445.name: Simplex Chithyola Banda
a3445.title: Minister of Finance of Malawi
a3445.speech: Echoed the RBM Governor's sentiments, calling for a national mindset shift anchored in Ubuntu — "one Malawi, one people, one nation"; viewed the conference as a potential turning point in Malawi's economic recovery; explained that the suspension of the ECF was a necessary step, taken through a delegation he led to the IMF, in order to renegotiate more realistic conditions post-2025 elections, noting that despite fulfilling several ECF requirements, some conditions — particularly fuel pricing adjustments — posed social risks and lacked public buy-in; stressed the need for homegrown solutions and tailor-made economic policies, affirming that Malawi's economic future depends on the collective efforts of its citizens.

a3445.speaker: Political party delegates at the PAC conference
a3445.name: Political party delegates at the PAC conference
a3445.speech: Raised pressing concerns regarding fiscal accountability and economic governance, including a lack of transparency in the utilisation of public debt, and voiced concerns over the devaluation of the Kwacha — noting that devaluation does not necessarily resolve the economic challenges it is assumed to address and "tends to have further negative ripple effects thereby exacerbating the cost of living of the ordinary Malawian".

a3445.speaker: Other delegates at the PAC conference
a3445.name: Other delegates at the PAC conference
a3445.speech: Emphasised the need for structural economic transformation, urging a shift from an agriculture-dominated economy toward a more diversified portfolio including mining and manufacturing, and highlighted the role of the diaspora, with calls for greater inclusion in national economic policymaking and a need to address the reported decline in remittances.

a3445.speaker: Participants from the private sector and professional associations/think tanks
a3445.name: Participants from the private sector and professional associations/think tanks
a3445.speech: Emphasised the importance of technocratic leadership in economic management, with consensus that interest rates and tax regimes should be managed based on sound economic principles rather than political influence, and stressed the need for a private-sector-led recovery strategy, particularly in agriculture, tourism and mining.

a3445.speaker: Civil society actors and media representatives at the PAC conference
a3445.name: Civil society actors and media representatives at the PAC conference
a3445.speech: Expressed strong reservations about the government's economic policies, particularly around debt management and currency devaluation; called for full public disclosure of the sources and terms of debt, questioned the effectiveness of past devaluation strategies, called for accountability at the highest levels of government and action on systemic corruption citing unfulfilled promises in the mining sector, scrutinised enforcement of labour protections such as the minimum wage, and debated the role and continued involvement of the IMF with divergent views on whether such partnerships enhance or erode Malawi's economic sovereignty.

a3566.speaker: Kouame Christophe Kouakou, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Cote d'Ivoire to Lebanon
a3566.name: Kouame Christophe Kouakou
a3566.title: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Cote d'Ivoire to Lebanon
a3566.speech: Presented the business environment in Cote d'Ivoire, marked by the particularly attractive character of the new 2018 investment code and the investment opportunities his country offers; and first recalled the excellence of the diplomatic relations that have existed between his country and Lebanon since they were established in 1961.

a3566.speaker: Kouame Christophe Kouakou, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Cote d'Ivoire to Lebanon
a3566.name: Kouame Christophe Kouakou
a3566.title: Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Cote d'Ivoire to Lebanon
a3566.speech: Underlined the significant contribution of the Lebanese community to the Ivorian economy; in his view the country's economic and social successes constitute a resounding call to invest in Cote d'Ivoire. He also stressed that investment promotion and trade exchanges are the key pillars of the work he has driven forward in his mission since taking up his post two years ago.

a3566.speaker: Panellists including Elie Yashouii (economics professor), Robert Geryessati (president of the Lebanese Federation of Businessmen), Aref Yassin (president of the Order of Engineers of Beirut) and Toufic Dabbousi (president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Tripoli)
a3566.name: Panellists including Elie Yashouii (economics professor)
a3566.title: Robert Geryessati (president of the Lebanese Federation of Businessmen), Aref Yassin (president of the Order of Engineers of Beirut) and Toufic Dabbousi (president of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Tripoli)
a3566.speech: Successively noted the legendary hospitality of Ivorians towards the Lebanese, thanks to Cote d'Ivoire's first president Felix Houphouet-Boigny and his worthy successor President Alassane Ouattara; in their view the Lebanese have found in Cote d'Ivoire a second homeland. They above all highlighted Cote d'Ivoire's exceptional economic performance, despite the economic crisis the world is going through.

a3634.speaker: Environmental Management Agency (EMA)
a3634.name: Environmental Management Agency (EMA)
a3634.speech: In 2024 reported an alarming surge in veld fires, with 982,964 hectares burnt — an increase of over 14 percent from the previous year, with Mashonaland West alone accounting for nearly half of the area lost.

a3634.speaker: Ntandokamlimu Nondo, EMA's acting director
a3634.name: Ntandokamlimu Nondo
a3634.title: EMA's acting director
a3634.speech: "These fires are no longer just an environmental hazard; they are a full-blown disaster. They cost the country over US$300,000 annually and impact almost every sector—agriculture, tourism, infrastructure, and environment." ; Pinpointed human activities, particularly in resettlement areas, as primary culprits, noting that 85 percent of fire incidents originate from these zones, and called for a coordinated national strategy, engaging government ministries, traditional leaders, and local communities.

a3634.speaker: Evelyn Ndlovu, Minister of Environment, Climate and Wildlife
a3634.name: Evelyn Ndlovu
a3634.title: Minister of Environment, Climate and Wildlife
a3634.speech: Launched the 2025 National Fire Week earlier this month, urging farmers to implement early fire suppression measures. "This is no longer a seasonal inconvenience. Veld fires destroy ecosystems, food security, and lives. We must work towards zero tolerance." She also emphasised the importance of curbing veld fires ahead of the 15th Conference of Contracting Parties (COP15) to the Convention on Wetlands, which Zimbabwe will host in Victoria Falls in July: "The world is watching. We must showcase a veld-fire-free Zimbabwe."

a3634.speaker: Fire risk assessments for 2025
a3634.name: Fire risk assessments for 2025
a3634.speech: Predict dire outcomes: 43 percent of the country faces a high risk of fires, with districts such as Marondera, Gweru, and Nyanga classified as extremely vulnerable.

a3634.speaker: Senator Sam Matema, chair of the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Environment
a3634.name: Senator Sam Matema
a3634.title: chair of the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Environment
a3634.speech: Highlighted the disproportionate impact on marginalised groups. "Women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities suffer the most when these fires strike. We must fulfill our constitutional duty to advocate for the vulnerable and protect our environment," he said, calling for targeted legislative efforts.

a3634.speaker: Chief Masendu of Matabeleland South, traditional leader
a3634.name: Chief Masendu of Matabeleland South
a3634.title: traditional leader
a3634.speech: "Our communities need to be at the forefront. Let's return to our roots—educating each other through community meetings, workshops, and campaigns."
