a3634.speaker: Lewis Radzire, Forestry Commission operations manager
a3634.name: Lewis Radzire
a3634.title: Forestry Commission operations manager
a3634.speech: Proposed an integrated fire management approach, encouraging farmers to form coalitions to pool resources and respond effectively to outbreaks. "We are finalizing a Statutory Instrument that decentralises fire management," Radzire revealed, emphasising the need for local authorities to act swiftly.

a3768.speaker: Trudi Nunoo, Project Director and Country Representative of FHI 360
a3768.name: Trudi Nunoo
a3768.title: Project Director and Country Representative of FHI 360
a3768.speech: Said the equipment would help improve diagnostics, detect outbreaks early, and enhance Ghana's capacity to respond more effectively to animal health threats: "We want to ensure they are not just received but used to full capacity." ; Said the project would also support the training of laboratory technicians to ensure proper handling and use of the donated equipment.

a3768.speaker: Dr Emmanuel Cudjoe, Chief Veterinary Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.name: Dr Emmanuel Cudjoe
a3768.title: Chief Veterinary Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.speech: Pledged that the equipment would be properly used and maintained: "We'll take good care of them. And the results they produce will be documented and shared to demonstrate that all investments made into strengthening animal health systems are yielding results."

a3768.speaker: Dr Emmanuel Cudjoe, Chief Veterinary Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.name: Dr Emmanuel Cudjoe
a3768.title: Chief Veterinary Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.speech: Called for stronger laboratory systems and more accreditation, noting Ghana currently has only one accredited veterinary lab: "But I assure you that in five years, we will not have only one."

a3768.speaker: Dr Edward Fenteng-Danso, Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.name: Dr Edward Fenteng-Danso
a3768.title: Deputy Chief Executive Officer of the Veterinary Services Directorate (VSD)
a3768.speech: Described the gesture as timely and essential: "The good news is that this donation is going to all 10 regions we are working with. This is a good gesture, and we must ensure the equipment is not left idle. We should justify this investment by increasing efficiency and output in our labs."

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president and former governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi
a3806.speech: has accused President Lazarus Chakwera of being out of touch with the reality facing Malawians, particularly the soaring poverty levels driven by a faltering economy, describing the current economic policies under Chakwera as a failure ; lambasted the President for his lack of proactive solutions to the country’s mounting crises: “Chakweranomics has never worked for Malawians.”

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president
a3806.speech: argued that the government’s reliance on foreign aid, rather than addressing fundamental issues such as foreign exchange shortages, fertilizer access, and food security, has only deepened the crisis ; contended that the President’s call for continued aid in response to Malawi’s growing fertilizer and food insecurity was misguided: “Instead of asking for help, the President should have started by holding accountable those responsible for these crises and implementing robust economic policies to safeguard the nation’s forex reserves.”

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president
a3806.speech: criticized the Chakwera administration for failing to create an environment conducive to investment and pointed out that the President should have prioritized investments in key forex-generating sectors, including mining, agriculture, and manufacturing: “The government should have been working to boost key sectors of the economy that could generate foreign currency and create jobs, not relying on begging bowls and short-term solutions.”

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president
a3806.speech: argued that Chakwera should have moved to revive Admarc, the Agricultural Development and Marketing Corporation, to ensure farmers had access to necessary inputs and a sustainable market for their produce: “Instead of waiting for international aid, the government should be strengthening its own institutions that can support the farmers who are at the heart of the economy.”

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president
a3806.speech: argued that the government’s approach to fuel importation contradicts basic economic principles and exposes the country’s vulnerability, claiming that the Chakwera administration’s fuel policy has further deepened the country’s foreign exchange crisis, making essential imports even more difficult to secure.

a3806.speaker: Dalitso Kabambe, UTM Party president
a3806.name: Dalitso Kabambe
a3806.title: UTM Party president
a3806.speech: accused the President of leading a government that is out of touch with the struggles of everyday Malawians, and expressed frustration with Chakwera’s continued assurances without tangible results: “It’s been nearly three years since this administration took office, yet we see no real change for the better. People are suffering, and instead of addressing the real issues, the President is busy with speeches that offer no hope for the future.”

a3806.speaker: Kondwani Nankhumwa, People’s Development Party (PDP) president
a3806.name: Kondwani Nankhumwa
a3806.title: People’s Development Party (PDP) president
a3806.speech: joined the chorus of discontent, describing the President’s recent national address as “empty” and devoid of any substantial plans for the country’s recovery.

a3844.speaker: Senior bank executive (anonymous)
a3844.name: Senior bank executive (anonymous)
a3844.speech: "We contributed to support humanitarian aid... The contributions were requested for the support of those displaced."

a3844.speaker: People close to the matter (anonymous)
a3844.name: People close to the matter (anonymous)
a3844.speech: According to people close to the matter, banks made donations proportional to the profits they made last year.

a3844.speaker: UN-OCHA
a3844.name: UN-OCHA
a3844.speech: According to UN-OCHA, an estimated 5.5 million people need emergency humanitarian assistance in Tigray Regional State.

a3844.speaker: Melaku Kebede, CEO of Hibret Bank
a3844.name: Melaku Kebede
a3844.title: CEO of Hibret Bank
a3844.speech: "We had taken time to discuss the issue within the Association... We contributed like any other industry that was asked to."

a3844.speaker: Yonas Zewde, head of the Addis Abeba City Administration's Communications Office
a3844.name: Yonas Zewde
a3844.title: head of the Addis Abeba City Administration's Communications Office
a3844.speech: Said a total of 1.5 billion Br was raised last week to support the federal army and humanitarian assistance efforts, with the remaining quarter of a billion Birr raised from private companies and businesspeople ; Disclosed that Ethiopian nationals abroad and others have also been raising funds, amounting to 200 million Br following the ceremony last week ; "The government budget alone can't sustain the rehabilitation process... We'll need support from businesspeople."

a3844.speaker: Billene Seyoum, the Prime Minister's press secretary
a3844.name: Billene Seyoum
a3844.title: the Prime Minister's press secretary
a3844.speech: Told CNN last week that the federal government has spent close to 100 billion Br on humanitarian efforts and rehabilitation in Tigray.

a3844.speaker: Humanitarian and recovery response plan prepared by the Amhara regional government
a3844.name: Humanitarian and recovery response plan prepared by the Amhara regional government
a3844.speech: According to the plan, financial support in the hundreds of millions of dollars is needed to respond to the humanitarian catastrophe and rehabilitation works.

a3911.speaker: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation
a3911.name: Cospas-Sarsat International Organisation
a3911.speech: Announced during its virtual meeting held on 13 June the formation of a specialised international working committee on artificial-intelligence applications within search-and-rescue satellite systems, following the success of the organisation's meetings held in Abu Dhabi from 27 May to 5 June 2025.

a3911.speaker: National Guard Command of the UAE, represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre
a3911.name: National Guard Command of the UAE
a3911.title: represented by the National Search and Rescue Centre
a3911.speech: Submitted the working paper on which the decision was based during the international committee's meetings, putting forward a pioneering technical proposal aimed at integrating artificial-intelligence technologies into the operations of the Mission Control Centre (MCC), so as to enhance the efficiency of space rescue systems and improve the speed and accuracy of the response to distress calls through the intelligent processing and integration of data across satellite networks.

a3911.speaker: Member states of Cospas-Sarsat
a3911.name: Member states of Cospas-Sarsat
a3911.speech: The Emirati initiative won wide praise from the member states for the innovation and forward-looking orientation it contained, reflecting the country's readiness and leadership in supporting international efforts to modernise the technical infrastructure of the Cospas-Sarsat system.

a3911.speaker: International Committee (Cospas-Sarsat)
a3911.name: International Committee (Cospas-Sarsat)
a3911.speech: Adopted a recommendation to form a joint working group chaired by the UAE to coordinate technical cooperation between member states and the relevant bodies and to develop artificial-intelligence tools linked to mission control centres ; praised the UAE's role, its qualitative contribution and its proactive initiatives in employing modern technologies to serve the goals of international humanitarian rescue.

a3934.speaker: Internal document from the US State Department (leaked)
a3934.name: Internal document from the US State Department (leaked)
a3934.speech: Lists Lesotho among 30 embassies and consulates that could be permanently closed; according to the document, the Trump administration, encouraged by the Elon Musk-backed Department of Government Efficiency, is reviewing American embassies and consulates with an eye toward closures, cost-saving consolidations, and “resizing” diplomatic missions worldwide; the document indicates the proposal originated from the State Department’s undersecretary for management and suggests posts were evaluated based on several criteria, including feedback from regional bureaus, consular workload, security ratings, and cost per US direct-hire employee.

a3934.speaker: Tammy Bruce, US State Department Spokesperson
a3934.name: Tammy Bruce
a3934.title: US State Department Spokesperson
a3934.speech: Declined to confirm or deny the plan. “I would suggest that you check with the White House and the President of the US as they continue to work on their budget plan and what they submit to Congress,” Bruce said. “The kinds of numbers and what we tend to see is reporting that is early or wrong, based on leaked documents from somewhere unknown.”

a3934.speaker: Experts (unnamed)
a3934.name: Experts (unnamed)
a3934.speech: Warn that the closure of the US Embassy in Lesotho could hinder diplomatic relations, reduce development support, and delay critical services like visa applications and consular assistance.

a3934.speaker: Analysts (unnamed)
a3934.name: Analysts (unnamed)
a3934.speech: Say reducing the US presence in the region could create a diplomatic vacuum and weaken America’s soft power, with China’s influence growing steadily across Africa.

a3934.speaker: Charles Blake, US Embassy Public Affairs Officer
a3934.name: Charles Blake
a3934.title: US Embassy Public Affairs Officer
a3934.speech: Told this publication that “No embassy or consulate closures have been announced, and operations continue as normal”.

a3934.speaker: Kutloano Pheko, Foreign Affairs Public Relations Officer
a3934.name: Kutloano Pheko
a3934.title: Foreign Affairs Public Relations Officer
a3934.speech: Said the issue remains just what it is, “a consideration”, and that it has not been diplomatically communicated.

a4319.speaker: Botswana and South Africa (joint declaration after ministers’ meeting in Pretoria)
a4319.name: Botswana and South Africa (joint declaration after ministers’ meeting in Pretoria)
a4319.speech: Declared their commitment to strengthening economic collaboration and reducing trade barriers between the two nations, identified that trade barriers are disrupting the free flow of goods, and committed to enhancing economic ties, improving communication on trade relations and identifying further areas of economic collaboration, including in manufacturing, agriculture and transport.

a4319.speaker: South African agricultural industry commentators and stakeholders
a4319.name: South African agricultural industry commentators and stakeholders
a4319.speech: Said that issues relating to import bans have raised the possibilities of a trade war.

a4319.speaker: South African Ministry of Trade, Industry and Competition (media statement)
a4319.name: South African Ministry of Trade
a4319.title: Industry and Competition (media statement)
a4319.speech: Said the two countries discussed “the promotion of trade and investment and committed to addressing key challenges hindering the full potential of economic cooperation between the two countries” ; “A central part of the discussions focused on addressing existing challenges including non-tariff barriers, regulatory obstacles and market access issues that have hindered trade growth. Both countries agreed to establish a bilateral working group to identify and resolve these challenges to ensure a fair and open trading environment. Both delegations expressed optimism about the future of their economic partnership and agreed to hold and sustain regular consultations to monitor progress and explore new areas of cooperation.”

a4397.speaker: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh, Director General of ANEFIP
a4397.name: Mahamoud Omar Guelleh
a4397.title: Director General of ANEFIP
a4397.speech: Stressed the importance of the meeting, which in his view will allow his institution to move forward with its programme to fight youth unemployment: "The Government of Djibouti, through the political vision of the President of the Republic H.E. Ismail Omar Guelleh, has committed to implementing several initiatives", including "the establishment of the employment access platform" allowing "young jobseekers to register and employer companies to find the skills they are looking for" ; told guests about the expansion of his institution, which now has "an employment directorate and human resources including some thirty advisers who guide and counsel young people looking for work" ; "In Djibouti, to take one or two examples, there will soon be the 'Aila Hotel', which will generate 200 jobs. The Salam group will also open two hotels... So the State, through the Ministry of Labour and ANEFIP, together with the national tourism agency, must prepare the staff who will work in these hotel establishments. The aim of this day was therefore to discuss with hoteliers to learn more about the profiles and the training they want... within four months at most."

a4397.speaker: Nancy Ostrowski, USAID representative in Djibouti, and Abdo Said Mohamed, head of the World Bank office in Djibouti
a4397.name: Nancy Ostrowski
a4397.title: USAID representative in Djibouti, and Abdo Said Mohamed, head of the World Bank office in Djibouti
a4397.speech: Each in turn pledged to support the youth-unemployment programme implemented in recent years by the government.

a4397.speaker: Omar Abdi Said, Minister of Labour in charge of formalisation and social protection
a4397.name: Omar Abdi Said
a4397.title: Minister of Labour in charge of formalisation and social protection
a4397.speech: Recalled that the strategies established by the Government during the COVID-19 period made it possible to protect jobs and preserve the continuity of activity in the hotel sector ; specified that the objective of the consultation meeting is "first to draw up an assessment of the hazards linked to employability in your sector of activity, and then to develop career-organisation policies specifically targeted at the under-used pool of skills represented by women and young people in the Republic of Djibouti" ; "Since my appointment at the head of this department, I have committed to listening to the grievances of employers and workers' representatives on all matters of common interest affecting the social partners, favouring dialogue and consultation. (...) The Republic of Djibouti is a country with a tourism vocation, recognised by all around the world. That is the challenge our strategic vision, stemming from that of the President of the Republic, H.E. Ismail Omar Guelleh, is meant to answer: to create a pool of jobs meeting international standards for hotels and related activities."

a4397.speaker: Youssouf Mohamed Eusman, Director General of the Hotel Europe
a4397.name: Youssouf Mohamed Eusman
a4397.title: Director General of the Hotel Europe
a4397.speech: "The workshop we were invited to today was very interesting; it dealt with the private sector and particularly the hotel business. As you know, the sector has a future in Djibouti. In the area of employment there are big challenges to meet. During this meeting with the Minister of Labour we were able to identify all the existing shortcomings. So the State and the international organisations that provide assistance have promised to take up this challenge. So, as a long-standing professional, I would like all the problems highlighted in this workshop to be taken up, and we are also at their disposal. I think it is very interesting and that we must move forward."

a4397.speaker: Iltireh Osman, director of projects at the Ministry of Labour, and Zahra Youssouf Kayad (USAID)
a4397.name: Iltireh Osman
a4397.title: director of projects at the Ministry of Labour, and Zahra Youssouf Kayad (USAID)
a4397.speech: Presented the employment access platform set up by ANEFIP, the World Bank's Skills project and USAID's hotel-sector programme dedicated to "Youth Employment" activities, allowing participating employers to understand these tools for strengthening the fight against unemployment.

a4397.speaker: Organisers of the meeting
a4397.name: Organisers of the meeting
a4397.speech: Said the recommendations identified will serve as input for the drafting of a report aimed at further strengthening youth employability in the hotel sector.

a4515.speaker: CTA (Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique)
a4515.name: CTA (Confederation of Economic Associations of Mozambique)
a4515.speech: Speaks of losses in the order of 400 million meticais from the closure of the commercial zone.

a4515.speaker: Ernesto Mausse, President of the Commerce Department of the CTA
a4515.name: Ernesto Mausse
a4515.title: President of the Commerce Department of the CTA
a4515.speech: Said the business sector in Xai-Xai estimates at more than 400 million meticais the losses arising from the two days of paralysis in the sector.

a4515.speaker: António Cossa, head of the beach administrative post
a4515.name: António Cossa
a4515.title: head of the beach administrative post
a4515.speech: Assured that legal mechanisms would be created to resolve the problem [of the occupation of the beach tourist zone].

a4580.speaker: Hector Sabi Mekire, head of the Kotchi public primary school (EPP Kotchi)
a4580.name: Hector Sabi Mekire
a4580.title: head of the Kotchi public primary school (EPP Kotchi)
a4580.speech: Expressed his delight at his school being chosen to host the launch of the campaign.

a4580.speaker: Dr Wilfrid Batcho, coordinator of the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases (PNLMT)
a4580.name: Dr Wilfrid Batcho
a4580.title: coordinator of the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases (PNLMT)
a4580.speech: Specifies that the campaign, organised by the PNLMT with the technical and financial support of RTI/ENVISION/USAID and the collaboration of the Ministry of Nursery and Primary Education (MEMP), covers 28 communes for a total of 662,967 children in the departments of Borgou-Alibori, Atacora-Donga, Zou-Collines and Mono-Couffo.

a4580.speaker: Dr Wilfrid Batcho, coordinator of the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases (PNLMT)
a4580.name: Dr Wilfrid Batcho
a4580.title: coordinator of the National Programme for the Fight against Communicable Diseases (PNLMT)
a4580.speech: Indicates that bilharzia, a parasitic disease, is transmitted to humans via small snails that live in rivers, which gives it the name of the disease of water soiled by faeces; he continues that the parasite infects humans by penetrating the skin in fresh water and causes lesions in the host organs through the accumulation of the parasites' eggs in the tissues of the urinary, digestive and genital systems over years.

a4727.speaker: Nigerian House of Representatives (resolution)
a4727.name: Nigerian House of Representatives (resolution)
a4727.speech: Has asked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other relevant agencies to explore alternative funding sources to fill the gaps left by the US Global Health Policy in financing essential programmes ; also mandated its Committees on Finance and Foreign Affairs to seek collaboration with other entities such as the World Health Organisation, the European Union, private foundations, and donor agencies.

a4727.speaker: Kwamoti Laori, member of the House of Representatives (PDP, Adamawa)
a4727.name: Kwamoti Laori
a4727.title: member of the House of Representatives (PDP, Adamawa)
a4727.speech: Stated that Nigeria would be significantly affected by several policies introduced by the US government under President Trump ; warned that many Nigerians who currently rely on aid from the US government are at risk if urgent steps are not taken by the Nigerian government to bridge the funding gap ; "An estimated 1.9 million Nigerians living with HIV/AIDS depend on free antiretroviral therapy provided by the United States. Other initiatives targeted at tuberculosis control, malaria treatment, maternal and child healthcare, family planning, and nutrition - aimed at reducing disease burdens and improving overall health outcomes in Nigeria - are under imminent threat due to funding cuts. The implication is that many Nigerians face death" ; described the role of US aid in Nigeria as vital and crucial to the collective well-being of Nigerians ; "These US-funded programmes play a vital role in addressing Nigeria's public health challenges. The implications of US policies on these initiatives will be crucial for future health outcomes in the coming days and months if nothing is done" ; "In 2023 alone, the United States invested over $600 million in health assistance in Nigeria. This funding supports various healthcare programmes, strengthens health systems, and addresses both current and future health security threats in the region."

a4727.speaker: Elon Musk, billionaire tasked with scaling down USAID
a4727.name: Elon Musk
a4727.title: billionaire tasked with scaling down USAID
a4727.speech: Has falsely accused USAID of being a "criminal" organisation.

a4727.speaker: Nigerian government (statement from President Bola Tinubu's office)
a4727.name: Nigerian government (statement from President Bola Tinubu's office)
a4727.speech: Admitted on Monday that the US government's actions would impact the country's healthcare system and announced several measures in response; at the Federal Executive Council meeting presided over by President Bola Tinubu, officials discussed the impact of Trump's policies, particularly in relation to HIV, tuberculosis, and malaria funding.

a4761.speaker: The top UN humanitarian official in Sudan
a4761.name: The top UN humanitarian official in Sudan
a4761.speech: Has welcomed the Government’s decision to extend the use of the Adre border crossing, a vital conduit for humanitarian assistance, for an additional three months.

a4884.speaker: Authorities in Raja, Western Bahr el Ghazal State
a4884.name: Authorities in Raja
a4884.title: Western Bahr el Ghazal State
a4884.speech: According to authorities in Raja, over 24,000 returnees from Sudan are facing dire need of humanitarian assistance in different camps in the County.

a4884.speaker: Gismallah Hassan Dahia, press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.name: Gismallah Hassan Dahia
a4884.title: press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.speech: Said the returnees from conflict-torn Sudan are mainly children, women, and elderly; added the returnees are arriving from Sudan daily to the areas of Siri-Malaga, Boro el Madina, Tamsah and Raja, having fled from the Zamzum refugee camp in El Dein town of Eastern Darfur via Kafia Kengi.

a4884.speaker: Gismallah Hassan Dahia, press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.name: Gismallah Hassan Dahia
a4884.title: press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.speech: Said the returnees have been lacking food and medicines for months now; "The returnees are in big number and have been lacking food. The International Comitte of the Red Cross had given them food assistance since last year. Even (those) in Boro - al Madina now, don't have food. The new arrivals of more than 950 people came here without anything, they facing issue of shelters, food and something to sleep on," he said.

a4884.speaker: Gismallah Hassan Dahia, press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.name: Gismallah Hassan Dahia
a4884.title: press secretary of the Raja County Commissioner
a4884.speech: According to him, the ongoing humanitarian challenges faced by returnees and displaced populations in South Sudan have been worsened by limited resources and support infrastructure.

a4884.speaker: United Nations (registration figures)
a4884.name: United Nations (registration figures)
a4884.speech: Since the fighting erupted in Khartoum, Sudan, the UN has registered more than 1 million people who have crossed into South Sudan, with 90% of them South Sudanese.

a4892.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a4892.name: Emmanuel Macron
a4892.title: President of France
a4892.speech: In 2023, President Macron unveiled yet another “new African strategy”, announcing a shift away from old models in favour of “equal partnership” and “sustainable development.”

a4892.speaker: Experts (unnamed, on uranium mining in Niger)
a4892.name: Experts (unnamed
a4892.title: on uranium mining in Niger)
a4892.speech: estimate that radiation levels near these mines exceed permissible limits by 100 times, while uranium concentrations in local drinking water reach 15 mg/L—500 times the safe threshold.

a4892.speaker: Studies (cited on cancer in Niger mining region)
a4892.name: Studies (cited on cancer in Niger mining region)
a4892.speech: indicate a rise in cancer cases in the region over the past two decades.

a4892.speaker: Environmental organizations (on the EACOP pipeline)
a4892.name: Environmental organizations (on the EACOP pipeline)
a4892.speech: warn that the project threatens to destroy 2,000 km of natural landscapes, including national parks and reserves, while displacing over 100,000 local residents.

a4892.speaker: The Oakland Institute
a4892.name: The Oakland Institute
a4892.speech: has accused Bolloré Group of illegal land seizures, environmental degradation, and human rights violations in several African countries.

a4892.speaker: 2024 Global Terrorism Index (report)
a4892.name: 2024 Global Terrorism Index (report)
a4892.speech: According to the 2024 Global Terrorism Index, over 50% of all terrorism-related deaths were recorded in the Sahel countries of Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso.

a4892.speaker: Aicha Dahou, journalist for Algerian TV1
a4892.name: Aicha Dahou
a4892.title: journalist for Algerian TV1
a4892.speech: “France has been plundering Africa for decades, extracting its riches—uranium, gold, and oil—and turning the continent into a nuclear testing ground, now drowning it in millions of tonnes of radioactive waste.”

a4892.speaker: Asmahan Soltan, Algerian journalist
a4892.name: Asmahan Soltan
a4892.title: Algerian journalist
a4892.speech: “France covers about 70percent of its electricity needs with uranium, the key fuel for its 50+ nuclear plants. It lights up its cities at the cost of millions of Nigeriens suffering from the consequences of uranium mining.”

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: Claims the difficulties in assisting this new wave of IDPs arriving by sea are great, speaks of a deep humanitarian crisis and calls for solidarity and humanitarian aid ; says the city may be unable to respond to the many displaced victims of the insurgency arriving there, and appreciates the help that arrives but asks for greater coordination.

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: On the conditions in which the displaced arrive: “The displaced people who have arrived in the last five days arrive in very difficult situations. Most of them arrive dehydrated, some come sick, feeling sick. We had a lady who gave birth in the boat. They arrive in a difficult situation, scared and with few belongings... Many people have no documents, they arrive with almost nothing. That is the situation.”

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: On whether they are receiving the necessary support: “Yes, they are receiving support. There are people from the [Paquitequete] neighbourhood, the neighbourhood secretary and some organisations, plus some volunteers. They are receiving some support, but not enough, because it took us by surprise. We were assisting the 12,000 IDPs who arrived in Metuge... They [newly arrived IDPs] are not yet receiving the necessary support they need. They have been receiving a snack meal, hot tea, but not real, solid food, food which actually feeds them. Some are being sent to families and others, the government is looking at what it will do with them.”

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: On psychological support: “The psychological support team was trained by two of our psychologists, two psychologist sisters. Four groups have already been trained and, in the last two days, a fifth group is being trained. So, this group is attending the camps where those who have been displaced for about two months have been sent. This team has not yet come to these people on the beach, because it is not relevant to give that support now... But the team is ready to give that support later. We are doing this work in Metuge, but the idea is to start this work in the neighbourhoods of Pemba, because there are many, many families there.”

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: On what he foresees for the city: “Pemba is already overcrowded. If this avalanche of refugees continues to arrive, we foresee a city completely flooded with people without having the necessary sanitary and physical conditions. I will not say that the population in Pemba has doubled, but it is said here that there are more than 80,000 displaced people in Pemba. So, imagine a small city that was not prepared for this. The more people arrive, the worse the situation gets. In terms of humanitarian assistance, it is very difficult... It is very hard work for humanitarian organizations and for the government itself.”

a4911.speaker: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa, Bishop of Pemba
a4911.name: Dom Luiz Fernando Lisboa
a4911.title: Bishop of Pemba
a4911.speech: On solidarity and coordination: “It is true that the support and solidarity of many people in society has grown, both individuals and groups... It is a pity that there is no concentration of forces. Much aid is too dispersed. For example, one group helps with 100 loaves, another with 200 and another with 300… If we put it all together, we could make food, rice or beans and ‘xima’. So, coordination is still lacking” ; “The people of Cabo Delgado, in the first place, are to be congratulated for their hosting, for their solidarity. Nobody is counting; everyone is sharing” ; “We are truly in a deep humanitarian crisis and we need solidarity. So, I want to invite people of good will to join groups of friends, businesspeople, to get in touch with us. We need support, we need help. There are a lot of people to be assisted and who need everything, but right now we are taking care of the most basic needs, which is food and a place to stay.”

a4944.speaker: Regional public and private sector leaders (East Africa Institutional Investors Forum)
a4944.name: Regional public and private sector leaders (East Africa Institutional Investors Forum)
a4944.speech: urged greater collaboration to align domestic capital with East Africa's long-term development goals, building on the strong foundations set by regional governments.

a4944.speaker: Aboubakar Massinda, Executive Vice-President for Energy and Infrastructure at Stanbic Bank Tanzania
a4944.name: Aboubakar Massinda
a4944.title: Executive Vice-President for Energy and Infrastructure at Stanbic Bank Tanzania
a4944.speech: "There is a growing alignment between public sector development goals and private sector capital flows." ; "This forum reflects our shared commitment to working in partnership with governments to deliver inclusive, sustainable infrastructure across the region."

a4944.speaker: Benedict Nkini, Vice-President for Financial Institutions at Stanbic Bank Tanzania
a4944.name: Benedict Nkini
a4944.title: Vice-President for Financial Institutions at Stanbic Bank Tanzania
a4944.speech: emphasised the bank's longstanding cooperation with government institutions: "For over thirty years, we have worked side by side with public and private stakeholders in Tanzania to structure investment solutions that deliver. We are now extending that collaborative spirit to the wider region."

a4944.speaker: Participants at the East Africa Institutional Investors Forum
a4944.name: Participants at the East Africa Institutional Investors Forum
a4944.speech: welcomed the progress made by governments to strengthen public investment systems, deepen capital markets and create enabling environments for public-private partnerships; noted that ongoing reforms have created a solid base to attract long-term investment, while estimates place East Africa's infrastructure financing needs at over 42 billion US dollars.

a4944.speaker: Aime Uwase, Director of Planning at the East African Community (EAC)
a4944.name: Aime Uwase
a4944.title: Director of Planning at the East African Community (EAC)
a4944.speech: said the forum was well-aligned with ongoing regional integration efforts: "The EAC Vision 2050 recognises infrastructure as a key driver of growth and this platform demonstrates the collective will to mobilise capital through joint action."

a4944.speaker: Githuku Mwangi, Transaction Advisor at CPF Capital and Advisory Services
a4944.name: Githuku Mwangi
a4944.title: Transaction Advisor at CPF Capital and Advisory Services
a4944.speech: praised the forum as a space for building shared understanding: "What we see here is not a critique, but an opportunity. East African economies have come far. Now it is about strengthening the collaboration between banks, fund managers and policymakers to ensure that all parts of the financial ecosystem work together."

a4944.speaker: Development finance institutions present at the forum
a4944.name: Development finance institutions present at the forum
a4944.speech: expressed willingness to provide concessional finance and technical assistance not to replace government efforts, but to support their effective implementation.

a4944.speaker: Forum organisers
a4944.name: Forum organisers
a4944.speech: "This forum is just the beginning." ; "The region has the vision, the institutions and the resolve. Our role is to listen, align and support that momentum."

a4957.speaker: Our Water, Our Right African Coalition (OWORAC)
a4957.name: Our Water
a4957.title: Our Right African Coalition (OWORAC)
a4957.speech: Has urged African governments to prioritize the human right to water and reject the growing influence of privatization across the continent; decried the devastating consequences of privatization on communities' access to safe and affordable water, urging leaders to adopt sustainable, public-centered water management systems.

a4957.speaker: Akinbode Oluwafemi, Executive Director of Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA)
a4957.name: Akinbode Oluwafemi
a4957.title: Executive Director of Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA)
a4957.speech: Called on governments to put people over profit: "Africa is facing a critical moment. The privatization of water services is a direct threat to the human right to water. It's time for our leaders to reject corporate control over water resources and take bold action to secure affordable, clean water for every citizen." ; stressed that privatization has consistently failed to deliver equitable access to water across Africa: "Water privatization only serves to line the pockets of corporations, while leaving our communities, especially the poor and marginalized, to suffer." ; "Governments must end their reliance on these failed models and instead invest in strong public water management."

a4957.speaker: OWORAC (press release co-signed by civil society leaders across the continent)
a4957.name: OWORAC (press release co-signed by civil society leaders across the continent)
a4957.speech: Pointed to alarming examples of privatization's toll on African nations; noted that multinational corporations, with the backing of financial institutions like the World Bank and IMF, are pushing privatization policies under the guise of development, schemes which have undermined public access to water and damaged public institutions tasked with providing essential services.

a4957.speaker: OWORAC (the group)
a4957.name: OWORAC (the group)
a4957.speech: Said that in Lagos, Nigeria, privatization efforts are being supported by international agencies such as USAID and the UK's FCDO who have displaced unionized workers and increased the threat of further privatization of water systems; "In Ghana, the reckless behavior of mining companies has caused widespread water pollution, with dangerous chemicals like mercury and cyanide leaching into rivers, endangering local communities"; said that in Senegal the French multinational Suez has taken over management of the water system, resulting in unreliable water access and rising costs, with Suez fighting back against unionized workers with heavy-handed tactics; noted Kenya is grappling with a new Water Amendment Act that has created conditions for privatization of water services, while Mozambique faces the looming threat of privatizing its national water utility; further noted that despite positive steps such as rollbacks of privatization efforts in Cameroon and Gabon, the fragility of public water systems in these countries continues to create openings for corporate takeover.

a4957.speaker: OWORAC's leaders
a4957.name: OWORAC's leaders
a4957.speech: Insist that the solution lies in empowering public water systems that are transparent, sustainable, and accountable to the people; called on African governments to invest in their public institutions, protect workers' rights, and engage communities in managing water resources; reiterated that water is a fundamental human right and must not be treated as a commodity for profit: "The fight against water privatization is a fight for the very dignity and survival of African communities."

a4957.speaker: Akinbode Oluwafemi, Executive Director of CAPPA
a4957.name: Akinbode Oluwafemi
a4957.title: Executive Director of CAPPA
a4957.speech: "We have the solutions right in front of us. Community-driven, public water management can ensure that every African has access to clean, safe water. We just need the political will to make it happen."

a5200.speaker: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (Fewsnet), update from the USAid programme
a5200.name: Famine Early Warning Systems Network (Fewsnet)
a5200.title: update from the USAid programme
a5200.speech: Sees the sustained depreciation of the Zimbabwe currency as a danger to food security for some low-income households.

a5219.speaker: Patrick Pouyanné, TotalEnergies CEO (quoted in a Bloomberg report)
a5219.name: Patrick Pouyanné
a5219.title: TotalEnergies CEO (quoted in a Bloomberg report)
a5219.speech: expressed confidence in July that Namibia would experience an oil boom similar to Guyana’s ; indicated that achieving acceptable production costs is challenging.

a5219.speaker: Maggy Shino, Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner (quoted by Bloomberg, noted by OilNOW)
a5219.name: Maggy Shino
a5219.title: Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner (quoted by Bloomberg, noted by OilNOW)
a5219.speech: “We are preparing the country to be an energy hub for the region.”

a5219.speaker: Maggy Shino, Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner (quoted in a Reuters report)
a5219.name: Maggy Shino
a5219.title: Namibia’s Petroleum Commissioner (quoted in a Reuters report)
a5219.speech: explaining that government is collaborating with operators, including Shell, TotalEnergies and Galp, to design a shared infrastructure plan that may involve an upscale version of the Kudu gas-to-power project.

a5219.speaker: Bloomberg (report)
a5219.name: Bloomberg (report)
a5219.speech: reported Namibia’s economy could potentially double or triple by 2027.

a5219.speaker: Wael Sawan, Shell CEO
a5219.name: Wael Sawan
a5219.title: Shell CEO
a5219.speech: told analysts last month that Namibia’s acreage is “very challenging” and that the lower permeability of the rock made extracting oil and gas harder ; “A lot of our focus is on figuring out whether we can find ways to be able to develop commercially investable projects.”

a5252.speaker: Mamane Issoufou, Police Controller General, Governor of the Maradi Region
a5252.name: Mamane Issoufou
a5252.title: Police Controller General, Governor of the Maradi Region
a5252.speech: Stated in launching the day that "the combined actions of terrorist groups against our country are exacting a heavy toll on our populations, jeopardising their livelihoods and heightening their vulnerability" ; "This unjust war imposed on us weighs heavily on public funds, with significant resources allocated to the defence of the territory," he acknowledged, before assuring that in response "the Government will continue to work for a swift return of security and peace across the entire territory by providing our defence and security forces with the means necessary to neutralise these terrorist groups" ; maintained that to overcome these challenges sustainably, "we must continue our partnership within the framework of implementing the humanitarian/development nexus in order to arrive at medium- and long-term solutions capable of preventing and mitigating their impact on vulnerable populations" ; said humanitarian action must align with the ideals of the refoundation and that communities must be at the heart of humanitarian action, while respecting dignity beyond relief ; "The Government, for its part, will pursue its efforts to assist people facing multiple difficulties linked in particular to epidemics, malnutrition, food insecurity, floods and forced population movements."

a5252.speaker: Mahamane Sani Tsayabou, Representative of the OCHA humanitarian coordination office in Maradi
a5252.name: Mahamane Sani Tsayabou
a5252.title: Representative of the OCHA humanitarian coordination office in Maradi
a5252.speech: Explained that the chosen theme is a call to decision-makers to use their position and influence to put an end to atrocities and humanitarian suffering, relying on the legal instruments of human rights, international humanitarian law, as well as the means at their disposal ; affirmed that "affected populations need our help right now and we must be able to better anticipate, with confidence, the onset and impact of certain shocks," while acknowledging that acting before a foreseeable shock is not only more effective, but also less costly than the traditional humanitarian response.

a5291.speaker: Valentine Rugwabiza, Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for the Central African Republic and Head of MINUSCA
a5291.name: Valentine Rugwabiza
a5291.title: Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for the Central African Republic and Head of MINUSCA
a5291.speech: "We are here to listen to you and hear from you, but also to appreciate all that you have achieved. Nothing is possible without peace and stability, and you are the actors of this peace and stability," the SRSG told local authorities, community leaders, and representatives of civil society organizations ; also informed them that this was the first-ever joint field visit in the mission's history, involving all members of the Diplomatic Corps and representatives from the Government of CAR.

a5291.speaker: Valentine Rugwabiza, Head of MINUSCA
a5291.name: Valentine Rugwabiza
a5291.title: Head of MINUSCA
a5291.speech: thanked the members of the CMOP for their contribution to the peace process: "You are the ones who went where you were told that conflicts were beginning. You are the ones who took the road to meet with the different communities and ensure that these conflicts did not take place. And where they had taken place, you reconciled the communities. So, I thank you, and I encourage you to continue this work."

a5291.speaker: Valentine Rugwabiza, Head of MINUSCA
a5291.name: Valentine Rugwabiza
a5291.title: Head of MINUSCA
a5291.speech: invited women to register in large numbers when the registration operations on the electoral lists begin: "You must register, and you must tell all your other sisters (...). Now, while making this appeal, I am aware of the problems that exist. There are several of you who do not have identity documents" ; indicated that, in partnership with UN-Women and the Central African Government, MINUSCA would support the women in obtaining their identity documents to be able to register on the electoral lists ; also informed that upon returning to Bangui the Mission would work with the ambassadors to see how, together, they could make the vocational training center for the youth a reality.

a5291.speaker: Nicolas Nzoyoum, Cameroonian Ambassador to the Central African Republic
a5291.name: Nicolas Nzoyoum
a5291.title: Cameroonian Ambassador to the Central African Republic
a5291.speech: stated that he was extremely happy to return to Kaga-Bandoro, more than 12 years after his last visit, and to witness the restoration of state authority and that the people are pleased with the work done by the United Nations and other international partners. "We see a population that is coming back to life, feeling more and more comfortable about resuming activities, and this is work that is only just beginning. So, we are expected to do more," he stressed.

a5291.speaker: Bruno Foucher, French Ambassador
a5291.name: Bruno Foucher
a5291.title: French Ambassador
a5291.speech: "We came here to see the progress made by the restoration of state authority in the provinces, and I believe that, as my colleague from Cameroon has just said, everything we have been able to visit today actually confirms the opinion that we had from Bangui that the state was redeploying and that MINUSCA was playing a very essential role in this redeployment. So, we made several visits... we were able to speak with the population, with women who asked us for some additional support, and I believe that, as my colleague Nicolas said, peace has returned, we feel it, people say it, and it is the first achievement without which we cannot do anything, and it is on this that we must build."

a5291.speaker: Diego Escalona Paturel, European Union Ambassador to the Central African Republic
a5291.name: Diego Escalona Paturel
a5291.title: European Union Ambassador to the Central African Republic
a5291.speech: praised the work of MINUSCA and the government. "I was really very impressed by what I saw, by the quality of the work that MINUSCA is doing in all its areas of responsibility, but also in infrastructure, and, as it has been said previously, I think that this is proof of the progress in terms of stabilization, securing the country, and that, thanks to these bases, we will be able to move forward towards development programs," he said.

a5291.speaker: Fraiture Sacha, Deputy Chief of Mission of the United States of America
a5291.name: Fraiture Sacha
a5291.title: Deputy Chief of Mission of the United States of America
a5291.speech: expressed his pride in seeing the positive impact of the projects funded by the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). "I am really proud to be here today because, after this visit, I can really realize that, well, there are good MINUSCA programs and we must also work with the European Union and the diplomatic community to improve the level of stability and also the empowerment of women (...) there are still many things to do," he pointed out.

a5291.speaker: Maxime Balalou, Minister of Communication and Media/Government Spokesperson
a5291.name: Maxime Balalou
a5291.title: Minister of Communication and Media/Government Spokesperson
a5291.speech: congratulated the populations for their resilience as well as for their contribution to the return of peace and the strengthening of social cohesion, while encouraging them to continue working to preserve peace and national unity with a view to ensuring the integral development of their community.

a5291.speaker: Local authorities, community and civil society leaders of Nana-Gribizi
a5291.name: Local authorities
a5291.title: community and civil society leaders of Nana-Gribizi
a5291.speech: praised the work done in partnership with MINUSCA and the United Nations country team, while asking them to continue proving their support because there are still some needs that require additional support.

a5291.speaker: Alvin Moussa Zavido, Mayor of Kaga-Bandoro, and Daniel Nguerelessio, President of the CLPR
a5291.name: Alvin Moussa Zavido
a5291.title: Mayor of Kaga-Bandoro, and Daniel Nguerelessio, President of the CLPR
a5291.speech: highlighted the fact that most young people are unemployed, which is a risk factor, because they are vulnerable and exposed to recruitment by armed groups that offer them an occupation. They advocated for the construction of a vocational training center to offer the Nana-Gribizi youth better professional prospects.

a5291.speaker: Agnes Diamdo, member of the Kaga-Bandoro City Council, speaking on behalf of the women
a5291.name: Agnes Diamdo
a5291.title: member of the Kaga-Bandoro City Council, speaking on behalf of the women
a5291.speech: deplored the low representation of women in decision-making bodies, particularly in the local administration, while acknowledging the remarkable work done in partnership with MINUSCA for the empowerment of women through various training projects and income-generating activities.

a5345.speaker: Somali officials
a5345.name: Somali officials
a5345.speech: Said diphtheria cases and deaths have risen sharply this year in Somalia, where the response has been curtailed by vaccine shortages and U.S. aid cuts.

a5345.speaker: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin, general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a5345.name: Hussein Abdukar Muhidin
a5345.title: general director of Somalia's National Institute of Health
a5345.speech: Said more than 1,600 cases, including 87 deaths, have been recorded, up from 838 cases and 56 deaths in all of 2024 ; separately echoed the health minister's comments about the closures of health centres.

a5345.speaker: Deka Mohamed Ali, mother of four children who contracted diphtheria
a5345.name: Deka Mohamed Ali
a5345.title: mother of four children who contracted diphtheria
a5345.speech: "My children got sick and I just stayed at home because I did not know it was diphtheria," she told Reuters from the bedside of her 3-year-old son Musa Abdullahi whose throat was swollen to the size of a lemon from the infection.

a5345.speaker: Ali Haji Adam, Somali Health Minister
a5345.name: Ali Haji Adam
a5345.title: Somali Health Minister
a5345.speech: Said the government had struggled to procure enough vaccines due to a global shortage and that U.S. aid cuts were making it difficult to distribute the doses it had ; "The U.S. aid cut terribly affected the health funds it used to provide to Somalia. Many health centres closed. Mobile vaccination teams that took vaccines to remote areas lost funding and now do not work."

a5345.speaker: U.S. State Department spokesperson
a5345.name: U.S. State Department spokesperson
a5345.speech: "The United States continues to provide lifesaving foreign assistance in Somalia," said when asked about the impact of its aid cuts in the country. "America is the most generous nation in the world, and we urge other nations to dramatically increase their humanitarian efforts."

a5345.speaker: U.S. government statistics
a5345.name: U.S. government statistics
a5345.speech: According to them, overall U.S. foreign assistance commitments to Somalia stand at $149 million for the fiscal year that ends on September 30, compared with $765 million in the previous fiscal year.

a5345.speaker: Save the Children (aid group)
a5345.name: Save the Children (aid group)
a5345.speech: Said last month that the closure of hundreds of health clinics in Somalia this year due to foreign cuts has contributed to a doubling in the number of combined cases of diphtheria, measles, whooping cough, cholera and severe respiratory infections since mid-April.

a5345.speaker: Amnesty International
a5345.name: Amnesty International
a5345.speech: Said that in 2024 Somalia's government allocated 4.8% of its budget to health, down from 8.5% the previous year.

a5345.speaker: Somalia's health ministry
a5345.name: Somalia's health ministry
a5345.speech: Did not respond to a question about the criticism from doctors and human rights activists over its limited funding of the health sector; it has said it is planning to launch a vaccination drive but has not given details when.

a5523.speaker: The State of School Feeding Worldwide report, UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a5523.name: The State of School Feeding Worldwide report
a5523.title: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a5523.speech: Said the surge marked a 30 percent increase in school meal coverage and signals a major shift toward domestic investment in education, nutrition and inclusive development ; “The African continent has seen the most significant rise of any region, with the number of children receiving school meals rising by over 30 percent from 66 million in 2022 to 87 million in 2024” ; cited Chad, Ethiopia, Madagascar and Rwanda as countries where the number of pupils receiving school meals have increased sixfold ; “Government investments in school meals in Sub-Saharan Africa have also increased, signalling a significant shift from reliance on foreign aid to recognising school meals as a strategic public investment in children’s education, health and broader national development” ; “Other governments such as Ethiopia and Burundi have doubled and tripled their respective contributions since 2022, while still receiving some funding from external sources.”

a5523.speaker: Eric Perdison, WFP Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa
a5523.name: Eric Perdison
a5523.title: WFP Regional Director for Eastern and Southern Africa
a5523.speech: “Sourcing food locally provides healthy, culturally appropriate meals for children while supporting smallholder farmers, driving economic growth and national development” ; “A meal at school is more than just giving food to a child; it is also an investment in the family, the community, and ultimately a country’s future.”

a5523.speaker: The State of School Feeding Worldwide report (WFP)
a5523.name: The State of School Feeding Worldwide report (WFP)
a5523.speech: Noted that despite progress, millions of children in fragile states such as the Democratic Republic of Congo, Somalia and South Sudan still lacked access to school meals due to low domestic funding and declining donor support.

a5523.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5523.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5523.speech: Said it would continue prioritising these settings to safeguard learning and nutrition.

a5607.speaker: Four sources (three diplomats and a Congolese official, anonymous)
a5607.name: Four sources (three diplomats and a Congolese official
a5607.title: anonymous)
a5607.speech: told Reuters that Congolese negotiators have dropped a demand that Rwandan troops immediately leave eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, paving the way for a U.S.-brokered peace agreement to be signed between the longtime foes on Friday. The sources asked not to be named due to the sensitivity of the talks.

a5607.speaker: Analysts and diplomats
a5607.name: Analysts and diplomats
a5607.speech: according to analysts and diplomats, Rwanda has sent at least 7,000 soldiers over the border in support of the M23 rebels.

a5607.speaker: Rwanda (government)
a5607.name: Rwanda (government)
a5607.speech: has long denied providing arms and troops to M23 and says it is acting in self-defence.

a5607.speaker: Sources (anonymous) / U.S.-prepared draft authenticated by diplomats
a5607.name: Sources (anonymous) / U.S.-prepared draft authenticated by diplomats
a5607.speech: told Reuters earlier this month that Washington was pushing for Rwanda to withdraw its troops before the deal’s signing, a pre-condition that was also included in a U.S.-prepared draft authenticated by diplomats.

a5607.speaker: Three sources (anonymous)
a5607.name: Three sources (anonymous)
a5607.speech: told Reuters that the new version of the agreement aims to obtain the withdrawal of Rwandan troops from eastern Congo over several months, while two of them said the withdrawal would be conditioned on operations against the FDLR.

a5607.speaker: Yolande Makolo, Rwandan government spokesperson
a5607.name: Yolande Makolo
a5607.title: Rwandan government spokesperson
a5607.speech: told Reuters on Thursday that under the agreement the “lifting of defensive measures in our border area” would be contingent upon the FDLR’s “neutralisation”.

a5607.speaker: Tina Salama, spokesperson for Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi
a5607.name: Tina Salama
a5607.title: spokesperson for Congolese President Felix Tshisekedi
a5607.speech: told Reuters that Kinshasa was intent on securing the “disengagement or total withdrawal” of Rwandan forces from Congolese territory.

a5607.speaker: State Department spokesperson
a5607.name: State Department spokesperson
a5607.speech: said it did not comment on ongoing diplomatic negotiations.

a5607.speaker: Technical experts from the two countries
a5607.name: Technical experts from the two countries
a5607.speech: initialed a draft peace agreement last week, saying it addressed issues related to territorial integrity, “a prohibition of hostilities” and the disengagement, disarmament and conditional integration of non-state armed groups.

a5752.speaker: Johannes Mururani, participant in the Commitment Walk
a5752.name: Johannes Mururani
a5752.title: participant in the Commitment Walk
a5752.speech: Told the group he was a violent man until he attended a male engagement programme on gender norms under the USAID Reach Namibia Project, and that he is now adamant about creating a safe environment: "Imagine a world where boys and girls can walk safely to school without fear of violence. A world where women can make decisions about their health and bodies without coercion. A world where men and women stand together as equals, united in the fight against gender-based violence and HIV."

a5752.speaker: Katamba Nanyemba, project coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a5752.name: Katamba Nanyemba
a5752.title: project coordinator of the Reach Namibia Project
a5752.speech: Said there is ample evidence linking gender-based violence and HIV: "It shows us that survivors of violence have often limited control over their sexual health, face power imbalances that prevent them from negotiating safer sex, and fear stigma that deters them from accessing critical services."

a5752.speaker: Bonifatius Wakudumo, Kavango East Governor
a5752.name: Bonifatius Wakudumo
a5752.title: Kavango East Governor
a5752.speech: Told the group that it is their duty as men to educate themselves and others about GBV, its root causes, and its impact on individuals: "It is believed that five in six men are not abusers. But where are they? Can they stand up and be counted? Can the one in six who are abusers change their ways? Can we raise a new generation based on equality? Change is not easy, and it does not happen overnight. But every step we take today is a step toward building a safer and more equitable future. Let us be unwavering in our commitment and courageous in our actions."

a5796.speaker: US Representatives Karen Bass, Hank Johnson, Barbara Lee and Ilhan Omar
a5796.name: US Representatives Karen Bass
a5796.title: Hank Johnson, Barbara Lee and Ilhan Omar
a5796.speech: All emphasised the need to do more for the partnership with Africa and Namibia in particular.

a5796.speaker: Hage Geingob, President of Namibia
a5796.name: Hage Geingob
a5796.title: President of Namibia
a5796.speech: Thanked the government of the United States of America for donations of Covid-19 vaccines, including Pfizer that was recently delivered to Namibia; outlined the challenges posed by Covid-19 and the efforts of government to fight the virus but also lauded in the same vein the unity of purpose, which has been demonstrated by world leaders and humanity at large.

a5796.speaker: Hage Geingob, President of Namibia
a5796.name: Hage Geingob
a5796.title: President of Namibia
a5796.speech: Underscored the fact that Namibia would continue to pursue an independent foreign policy, consistent with her national interests and developmental objectives – and welcomed the possibility of Namibia benefiting from a second Compact under the Millennium Challenge Corporation.

a5796.speaker: Namibian delegation
a5796.name: Namibian delegation
a5796.speech: Informed that the filmmaking industry was receiving increasing priority and the Namibian government was keen to pursue opportunities with Starz; members of the delegation made sector contributions about growing exports to the US, unlocking opportunities for development finance, agriculture, logistics, mining and renewable energy, with an emphasis on green hydrogen.

a5829.speaker: Sources (anonymous)
a5829.name: Sources (anonymous)
a5829.speech: According to sources, the US government had issued a stop-work order, but the organization’s decision to lay off such a large number of employees has raised eyebrows.

a5829.speaker: Project Hope Namibia officials (non-response)
a5829.name: Project Hope Namibia officials (non-response)
a5829.speech: When approached for comment, officials from Project Hope Namibia requested more time to respond to the matter.

a5829.speaker: George Khakhi, Executive Director of the Employers Consultative Association of Malawi (ECAM)
a5829.name: George Khakhi
a5829.title: Executive Director of the Employers Consultative Association of Malawi (ECAM)
a5829.speech: Has described the layoffs as "unfortunate" and has appealed to the Malawi government to create more job opportunities to support the affected workers.

a5868.speaker: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah, Lead Negotiator for Ghana and Co-facilitator for Ghana's National Adaptation Plans (NAPs)
a5868.name: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah
a5868.title: Lead Negotiator for Ghana and Co-facilitator for Ghana's National Adaptation Plans (NAPs)
a5868.speech: Disclosed to GBC in Azerbaijan that parties failed to agree on texts regarding the New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG): "We spent almost the whole week trying to go through the same things we've gone through the past two years in those workshop format" ; said that one of the major objectives of COP 29 is to have a decision that is going to take us forward, starting from 2025 to implement climate finance as a replacement of the 100 billion-Dollar-goal that we already had ; said until texts have been agreed on for ministers to endorse, "It will just be talking, and that is not negotiations" ; described the financing issue as a "Do or die" affair, as 1.3 trillion Dollars annually is needed from developed countries to address the climate impacts facing developing ones ; mentioned the contending issues that hindered progress during the first week as the definition of climate finance, the amount, contributors and the composition of the funds.

a5868.speaker: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah, Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.name: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah
a5868.title: Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.speech: Explained that developing countries see the definition of climate finance as very important because "we've been duped before, where Overseas Development Assistance, ODA's and other things that were not climate finance were branded as such and being accounted for as part of the 100 billion dollars promised during the Copenhagen climate summit" ; noted, "Let us all agree on what constitutes climate finance, so that all of us (developed and developing countries) will be on the same page, the same understanding when it comes to the definition."

a5868.speaker: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah, Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.name: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah
a5868.title: Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.speech: Said the quantum of the money needed annually for developing countries is in trillions of dollars, which he believes "our partners don't agree" with because they think the amount is too huge, hence contributing to the delay in negotiations; explained that the demand by developing countries regarding the amount is based on some assessments, compelling them to demand the 1.3 trillion dollars as the starting amount.

a5868.speaker: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah, Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.name: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah
a5868.title: Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.speech: Though he agrees to proposals by others that contributors to the fund should be widened, referenced the Paris Agreement, which says "Developed country parties are supposed to provide climate finance for developing members to address their climate needs" ; said developing countries want public climate financing and not loans and other instruments that would increase their debt burden.

a5868.speaker: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah, Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.name: Dr Antwi Boasiako Amoah
a5868.title: Lead Negotiator for Ghana
a5868.speech: Said the COP presidency will provide guidance about the text he had and move it up from there; expressed optimism that with technical negotiations, it's possible to agree on texts within two days, "for ministers to take it up from there. Remember that climate finance can be the last thing to be agreed on, sometimes after the summit has concluded."

a5885.speaker: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and African National Congress (ANC) members of parliament
a5885.name: Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) and African National Congress (ANC) members of parliament
a5885.speech: In South Africa's parliament, nearly came to physical blows over why (and how) their government had allowed this to happen - both the collapse of civil order in Zimbabwe as well as the sudden flood of desperate people into South Africa.

a5885.speaker: Democratic Alliance speakers
a5885.name: Democratic Alliance speakers
a5885.speech: Insisted the government had to take responsibility for the urgent needs of the growing throng near the border regardless of who had caused it.

a5885.speaker: Freedom Front Plus
a5885.name: Freedom Front Plus
a5885.speech: Hinted darkly that - within the week - mobs would be looting farms or much worse in the northern part of the country in their growing desperation.

a5885.speaker: Foreign diplomats in Pretoria (joint demarche representing some two dozen foreign missions)
a5885.name: Foreign diplomats in Pretoria (joint demarche representing some two dozen foreign missions)
a5885.speech: Weighed in with a joint demarche to the South African government urging urgent South African government efforts to restore order and to take charge of the circumstances of the refugees by providing basic food, shelter and sanitary conditions - lest things degenerate any further.

a5885.speaker: UN High Commissioner for Refugees
a5885.name: UN High Commissioner for Refugees
a5885.speech: Announced that the number of people in the 10 camps now set up across the area had reached an incredible half a million people in less than a month.

a5885.speaker: South African Communist Party youth wing (communique)
a5885.name: South African Communist Party youth wing (communique)
a5885.speech: Issued a communique that denounced "western nations for fermenting [sic] the violence in Zimbabwe and spreading baseless rumours about the need to flee a comradely progressive nation", thereby "contributing to the spread of disease, the scarcity of food and the demands on hard-pressed medical personnel to preserve the benefits of the popular socialist revolution".

a5885.speaker: Alliance for Economic Progress in Southern Africa (Aepsa)
a5885.name: Alliance for Economic Progress in Southern Africa (Aepsa)
a5885.speech: Decried the reluctance of the South African government to do anything to limit the collapse of security and order in Zimbabwe, thereby contributing to the cessation of most major mining and industrial operations north of the Limpopo River.

a5885.speaker: Investigative journalist at The Daily Maverick
a5885.name: Investigative journalist at The Daily Maverick
a5885.speech: Discovered that major funders of Aepsa included Gupta family business interests, Lonmin, the Chinese Infrastructure Investment Bank, Anglo American, several prominent black economic empowerment mining groups, and a number of Russian mining houses.

a5885.speaker: General "Giant", Zimbabwean general
a5885.name: General "Giant"
a5885.title: Zimbabwean general
a5885.speech: Optimistically declared the fighting was now over; said he would welcome back all of his compatriots who had fled the recent fighting and urged international aid agencies to move their bases of operations into Zimbabwe itself in order to attract returnees, rather than across the northern rim of South Africa.

a5885.speaker: Donald Trump
a5885.name: Donald Trump
a5885.speech: Offered unsolicited advice in an internationally broadcast interview on the BBC that South Africa should build a wall all along the border and then simply round up all the new migrants and forcibly repatriate them back to their home nation.

a5885.speaker: Several senior South African government officials
a5885.name: Several senior South African government officials
a5885.speech: Were reported in the Sunday papers to have agreed that such a plan - building a border wall and forcibly repatriating the migrants - was both feasible and probably necessary.

a5885.speaker: The South African Presidency
a5885.name: The South African Presidency
a5885.speech: Quickly overruled these comments, explaining the press had cynically and typically misinterpreted some chance comments partially overheard from officials attending a wedding celebration the previous day, once they had heard The Donald's remarks.

a5885.speaker: Analysts
a5885.name: Analysts
a5885.speech: Explained this result represented a serious protest vote against an ANC that had long believed that province was secure for it in electoral terms, come what may.

a5885.speaker: South African Cabinet wordsmith/spinmeister (speaking in camera)
a5885.name: South African Cabinet wordsmith/spinmeister (speaking in camera)
a5885.speech: Said that no matter what choice they made, the outcome would be "less than optimal".

a5885.speaker: Nigeria and several other African nations
a5885.name: Nigeria and several other African nations
a5885.speech: Urgently called for African Union and UN Security Council meetings to discuss the now-widening crisis.

a5922.speaker: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (announcement)
a5922.name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (announcement)
a5922.speech: Announced, in response to the serious humanitarian crisis affecting Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Mali, that a high-level ministerial donors' conference would be held on 26 October, organised in collaboration with the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC).

a5922.speaker: United Nations data
a5922.name: United Nations data
a5922.speech: According to United Nations data, nearly 33 million people in the region need humanitarian assistance and protection, including about 11 million displaced persons and refugees in the Sahel and Lake Chad region.

a5922.speaker: Dr Abdullah Al Rabeeah, General Supervisor of the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief)
a5922.name: Dr Abdullah Al Rabeeah
a5922.title: General Supervisor of the King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Centre (KSrelief)
a5922.speech: “We recognise the importance of supporting the populations of the Sahel and Lake Chad regions. This conference is a crucial step towards mobilising the necessary resources and forging partnerships in order to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs in these regions. Together, we can bring hope and relief to millions of people.”

a5922.speaker: Hissein Brahim Taha, Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5922.name: Hissein Brahim Taha
a5922.title: Secretary General of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC)
a5922.speech: Said he was “proud of the role” they play in implementing the resolution of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers ; “To that end, I call on the OIC's donor member states, donor institutions and international partners to seize this opportunity and to provide the financial resources needed to help improve the conditions of vulnerable communities in these troubled regions.”

a5922.speaker: Joyce Msuya, Acting UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a5922.name: Joyce Msuya
a5922.title: Acting UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs and Emergency Relief Coordinator
a5922.speech: “The Sahel and the Lake Chad basin are facing an unprecedented crisis” ; “this conference represents a crucial opportunity for the international community and the affected countries to come together to mobilise more resources and more support – not only for the immediate humanitarian response, but to help the region emerge from the crisis and realise its enormous potential.”

a5922.speaker: Filippo Grandi, United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a5922.name: Filippo Grandi
a5922.title: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
a5922.speech: Said it is imperative to “redouble efforts to support forcibly displaced populations as well as the communities that host them” ; “We express our gratitude to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to the OIC and to our partners for their efforts to mobilise the attention and the resources needed to fill the serious funding shortfall affecting the region, in order to come to the aid of refugees and vulnerable populations.”

a6297.speaker: Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a6297.name: Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS)
a6297.speech: Demands 9 billion birr to assess humanitarian assistance in the 4 regions affected by conflict and violence.

a6297.speaker: ERCS assessment on the current conflict and violence
a6297.name: ERCS assessment on the current conflict and violence
a6297.speech: According to the assessment, a total of 0.53 million people are in need of humanitarian assistance in Tigray, Amhara, SNNP and Benishangul-Gumuz regions which requires 9 Billion Ethiopian Birr to provide general and supplementary food, non-food items water and sanitation services and other essential.

a6297.speaker: National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC) report of September 2020
a6297.name: National Disaster Risk Management Commission (NDRMC) report of September 2020
a6297.speech: Indicates that flood has also affected 1,095,358 people out of which 313,179 people were displaced across the country.

a6297.speaker: IRC
a6297.name: IRC
a6297.speech: Targeted to support 2,534,297 peoples affected in the four regions, IRC has called its partners and volunteers to raise 233,090,712 million dollar fund. ; IRC planned to support Western Tigray and North Gondar 646,462 population, Central, S/eastern, N/western and Eastern Tigray (22% from total affected 1,280,094), Southern Tigray, North wello and zone 2 of Afar (394,645), Metekel zone (336,823), Konso, Alle, Derashe and Bench Shoko of SNNP (204,493).

a6297.speaker: IRC
a6297.name: IRC
a6297.speech: Suggests enhancement of the culture of nonviolence through provision of peace education to increase peaceful coexistence among people, better coordination and collaboration among humanitarian actors to address ever increasing humanitarian actors, strengthening ERCS's emergency preparedness and response capacity at all level for a better living.

a6407.speaker: Internal Trump administration memo on foreign aid (seen by Reuters)
a6407.name: Internal Trump administration memo on foreign aid (seen by Reuters)
a6407.speech: Calls for funding fewer areas that it views as better aligned with U.S. geopolitical interests; argues the current U.S. foreign aid structure is too broad, too costly and has failed to reduce the dependency of some nations on U.S. assistance, and says funding should be allocated with a narrower, strategic focus: "This blueprint proposes a re-imagined U.S. international assistance structure and set of operating principles that promises measurable returns to America while also projecting American soft power, enhancing our national security; and countering global competitors including China" ; calls for the elimination of nearly two dozen USAID bureaus and for renaming the agency the U.S. Agency for International Humanitarian Assistance, with the new "specialized" body embedded in the State Department and its mandate limited to humanitarian assistance, disaster response, global health and food security; also proposes that any "politically-oriented programs," such as democracy promotion, religious freedom and women's empowerment, be moved to the State Department to handle directly. The memo was signed by Kenneth Jackson and Jeremy Lewin.

a6407.speaker: President Donald Trump and Elon Musk
a6407.name: President Donald Trump and Elon Musk
