a6407.speech: Say the federal government misuses taxpayer money for causes that do not advance U.S. interests.

a6407.speaker: Source familiar with the document (anonymous)
a6407.name: Source familiar with the document (anonymous)
a6407.speech: Said the internal memo will be sent to U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio for review.

a6407.speaker: Politico
a6407.name: Politico
a6407.speech: The memo was first reported by Politico.

a6407.speaker: State Department spokesperson
a6407.name: State Department spokesperson
a6407.speech: "We are committed to implementing President Trump and Secretary Rubio's foreign policy objectives by being as innovative, nimble, and focused as possible," the spokesperson said when asked about the memo.

a6407.speaker: Federal judge (court ruling)
a6407.name: Federal judge (court ruling)
a6407.speech: On Tuesday blocked Musk and the Department of Government Efficiency from proceeding with shutting down USAID, saying their efforts to close the agency likely violated the U.S. Constitution.

a6407.speaker: USAID's new leaders (internal USAID email seen by Reuters)
a6407.name: USAID's new leaders (internal USAID email seen by Reuters)
a6407.speech: Said one of the key priorities would be to administer the around 1,000 ongoing life-saving humanitarian aid programs: "We are committed to ensuring ongoing programs remain functional and can service beneficiaries in need" ; said the other priorities are to ensure the "safety, dignity and productivity" of USAID personnel during the transition and to work with Congress and Rubio to formulate a vision for how USAID is handed over to the State Department.

a6521.speaker: The Wall Street Journal (WSJ), citing people familiar with the matter
a6521.name: The Wall Street Journal (WSJ)
a6521.title: citing people familiar with the matter
a6521.speech: Reported that Liu was taken away after returning to Beijing in late July from an overseas work trip.

a6521.speaker: China's State Council Information Office and the Chinese Communist Party International Liaison Department
a6521.name: China's State Council Information Office and the Chinese Communist Party International Liaison Department
a6521.speech: Did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment.

a6585.speaker: Wallace Bain, First Counsellor of the United States Embassy in Mali
a6585.name: Wallace Bain
a6585.title: First Counsellor of the United States Embassy in Mali
a6585.speech: Stressed that the programme will respond to needs for protection, access to water, sanitation and the promotion of hygiene.

a6585.speaker: Elmedhi Ag Wakina, Director of Programmes of the Malian Association for Survival (AMSS)
a6585.name: Elmedhi Ag Wakina
a6585.title: Director of Programmes of the Malian Association for Survival (AMSS)
a6585.speech: Maintains that this programme responds to a volatile security situation in the three regions of Mopti, Gao and Ménaka, marked by serious human rights violations; cites data from actors involved in the gender-based violence information system which, according to him, identified 4,062 incidents between July and September 2023, of which 36% concern cases of sexual violence.

a6585.speaker: Elmedhi Ag Wakina, Director of Programmes of AMSS
a6585.name: Elmedhi Ag Wakina
a6585.title: Director of Programmes of AMSS
a6585.speech: Announces that this programme will adopt a multisectoral approach to strengthen the protection of children, combat gender-based violence and provide psychosocial assistance to survivors of such violence: "It will integrate a dimension of awareness-raising and prevention against the dangers of explosive devices," adding that it will respond to the WASH needs of people displaced by the crisis; according to him, adapted sanitation infrastructure (separate latrines, equipment for people with disabilities) will be put in place in schools and communities, along with gender-adapted hygiene awareness campaigns to promote practices that reduce health risks.

a6585.speaker: Terms of reference of the programme (document)
a6585.name: Terms of reference of the programme (document)
a6585.speech: "Of these incidents, 36% concern cases of sexual violence," the programme's terms of reference state.

a6585.speaker: Dr Abdoulaye Guindo, Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development of Mali
a6585.name: Dr Abdoulaye Guindo
a6585.title: Secretary General of the Ministry of Health and Social Development of Mali
a6585.speech: Went on to say that the protection, water, hygiene and sanitation programme, funded by USAID's humanitarian affairs bureau, will respond to the critical needs of vulnerable people in the centre and the north, and will mitigate the consequences of the security and humanitarian crisis afflicting these regions.

a6672.speaker: Nicolas Maduro, Venezuelan President
a6672.name: Nicolas Maduro
a6672.title: Venezuelan President
a6672.speech: Accuses the United States of America of sending warships to the waters off Venezuela and says the United States wants to appropriate the country's natural resources ; announced, at an event broadcast by the state channel Venezuelan Television, that the United States had sent eight warships and 1,200 missiles to the country's coast ; rejected Washington's argument that this is an operation to combat drug trafficking, describing it as a story ; accused the US of wanting to appropriate oil, gas and gold, after reiterating that his country holds the fourth largest gas reserves in the world and one of the largest global reserves of gold.

a6672.speaker: Washington (US government)
a6672.name: Washington (US government)
a6672.speech: Argues that it is an operation to combat drug trafficking.

a6672.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6672.name: Donald Trump
a6672.title: US President
a6672.speech: Announced on social media that the US Armed Forces had carried out a strike against a group of narcoterrorists from Tren de Aragua, a terrorist organization involved in drug trafficking, human trafficking, acts of violence, homicide and terror in the US, which according to Trump were in international waters transporting illegal narcotics on their way to the United States.

a6736.speaker: Janine Lélis, Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.name: Janine Lélis
a6736.title: Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.speech: The minister listed a series of measures already adopted to increase effectiveness and motivation and to ensure the readiness of the Armed Forces, but says that it is necessary to continue doing more to keep pace with the evolution of the concept of national defence. “In fact, defence has come to include issues related to the maritime security needed to guarantee global supply chains, the fight against piracy and against human trafficking, cyber defence and humanitarian aid, responses to natural disasters in the face of climate change, among others. All these issues are included in our concerns, because our archipelago's economy depends greatly on maritime trade and on tourism,” she states.

a6736.speaker: Janine Lélis, Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.name: Janine Lélis
a6736.title: Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.speech: The holder of the Defence portfolio hopes to count on the entry into service of the vessel Guardião, announced as coming “soon”, the arrival of an aircraft for the Coast Guard, the inclusion of drones in Armed Forces operations, and the training of military personnel in the field of surveillance.

a6736.speaker: Janine Lélis, Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.name: Janine Lélis
a6736.title: Minister of Defence of Cabo Verde
a6736.speech: “We need to ensure that the population feels part of the process of national security and defence, and that is everyone's mission. It is in this sense that once again I emphasise the campaign we intend to launch this year in relation to compulsory military service, precisely in order to show: that it is worth fighting for the homeland; the benefits of a military career; and to promote the opportunities for professional training and in the academies,” she points out.

a6736.speaker: António Duarte Monteiro, Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Cabo Verde (CEMFA)
a6736.name: António Duarte Monteiro
a6736.title: Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Cabo Verde (CEMFA)
a6736.speech: “I could not fail to allude to one of the greatest challenges the institution is currently experiencing, linked to the weak uptake of military service among young people, especially on the island of Santiago, which has brought difficulties in filling the ranks of the Armed Forces. We await with anticipation the result of the study commissioned by the Government, which will bring us answers as to the causes of this weak uptake and proposals for solutions,” he notes.

a6736.speaker: António Duarte Monteiro, Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Cabo Verde (CEMFA)
a6736.name: António Duarte Monteiro
a6736.title: Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Cabo Verde (CEMFA)
a6736.speech: On the same occasion, the CEMFA reaffirmed that the resumption of operations with the vessel Guardião is imminent, the repair process having already begun.

a6957.speaker: Admassie Tikuye, farmer displaced from Qobo, North Wello
a6957.name: Admassie Tikuye
a6957.title: farmer displaced from Qobo, North Wello
a6957.speech: "I'll try to go there," he told Fortune, of his hope to move to Addis Abeba where one of his daughters lives.

a6957.speaker: Officials from the Amhara Regional State
a6957.name: Officials from the Amhara Regional State
a6957.speech: According to officials from the regional state, the war left close to 300,000ht of land in the Amhara region unploughed this year, including 67 weredas in the regional state.

a6957.speaker: Esayas Lemma, director of crop development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.name: Esayas Lemma
a6957.title: director of crop development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.speech: Said that in two zones of Afar Regional State, constituting 14 weredas, 17,000ht of land was not cultivated as over half a million people were displaced. "The major causes for the loss of crops is looting of agricultural inputs, harvested products and the inability of farmers to tend to their farmlands as they are displaced. Those cultivated are left vulnerable to weeds, flooding and disease." ; Points out that the farmers themselves will be the worst affected by the developments, as close to 75pc of the output is a product of subsistence farming.

a6957.speaker: Esayas Lemma, director of crop development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.name: Esayas Lemma
a6957.title: director of crop development at the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.speech: "We're considering outputs from Tigray as a total loss. We're not expecting anything anymore."

a6957.speaker: Report from the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.name: Report from the Ministry of Agriculture
a6957.speech: A loss of 14.5 million quintals of crops (13pc of annual production) is projected in Amhara Regional State alone, according to a report from the Ministry of Agriculture.

a6957.speaker: Ayalnesh Fisseha, 40, displaced farmer from Qobo
a6957.name: Ayalnesh Fisseha
a6957.title: 40, displaced farmer from Qobo
a6957.speech: "We need help from the government," Ayalnesh pleaded.

a6957.speaker: Gizachew Muluneh, head of communications for the Amhara regional government
a6957.name: Gizachew Muluneh
a6957.title: head of communications for the Amhara regional government
a6957.speech: Says the administration delivers food to internally displaced sheltered places like Dessie; however, as the war spreads, it has become challenging to continue, and the government's effort to reach out to the population in Dessie and Combolcha was discontinued beginning last week.

a6957.speaker: Elias Gutu, owner of an agro-processing company exporting sesame
a6957.name: Elias Gutu
a6957.title: owner of an agro-processing company exporting sesame
a6957.speech: "We've lost all communications, and we don't know what's happening besides hearsay," Elias told Fortune; his company has been forced to cease operations as supplies have been cut off and is exploring exporting coffee until things return to "normal."

a6957.speaker: Seifu Assefa, agricultural expert who served at the Ministry of Agriculture for eight years
a6957.name: Seifu Assefa
a6957.title: agricultural expert who served at the Ministry of Agriculture for eight years
a6957.speech: Says the provision of farm inputs and technology should be given attention. "When the displaced farmers move back to their land, they might not find much. Seeds and technical support should be provided to rehabilitate the farmland."

a6965.speaker: Prince Moye, Bong County Senator
a6965.name: Prince Moye
a6965.title: Bong County Senator
a6965.speech: "The Spanish doctors will perform different surgeries at the C.B Dunbar Hospital in Gbarnga and the health center in Palala."

a6965.speaker: Prince Moye, Bong County Senator
a6965.name: Prince Moye
a6965.title: Bong County Senator
a6965.speech: According to the Bong County Lawmaker, the withdrawal of USAID is hugely affecting the Health and Education Sectors, prompting the need for short-term intervention, especially in health.

a6965.speaker: Prince Moye, Bong County Senator
a6965.name: Prince Moye
a6965.title: Bong County Senator
a6965.speech: Lauded the "Physicians and Doctors without Borders" for the partnership, and affirmed his office's full support during the five-day stay of the doctors in the country.

a6965.speaker: Dr. Ayun Cassell, Director of the organization
a6965.name: Dr. Ayun Cassell
a6965.title: Director of the organization
a6965.speech: "The surgical outreach is targeting different health complications, including hernia, hydrocele, and other general surgeries targeting about one hundred fifty patients."

a6965.speaker: Dr. Antonio Satorras, Team Head of the delegation
a6965.name: Dr. Antonio Satorras
a6965.title: Team Head of the delegation
a6965.speech: "The team was pleased to be in Liberia to perform such a critical task."

a6971.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary General
a6971.name: Antonio Guterres
a6971.title: UN Secretary General
a6971.speech: Said Russia's invasion of Ukraine one year ago brought "hell" to the Ukrainian people via "widespread death, destruction and displacement" ; "Life is a living hell for the people of Ukraine" ; said around 17.6 million people, or 40 percent of the Ukrainian population, needs humanitarian assistance and protection, while 30 percent of the jobs in the country have been wiped out ; said more than eight million Ukrainians have fled to other parts of Europe and another 5.4 million are internally displaced, "a displacement crisis not seen in Europe in decades" ; added that half of Ukrainian children have been forced from their homes and face higher risks of violence, abuse and exploitation ; noted that the UN Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights has already documented "dozens" of cases of sexual violence against men, women and girls tied to the war ; pointed out that the council has met 40 times on Ukraine.

a6971.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary General
a6971.name: Antonio Guterres
a6971.title: UN Secretary General
a6971.speech: Told the council the world needs peace "in line with the UN Charter and international law" ; "As we work for peace... protection of civilians must remain the top priority."

a6971.speaker: Antonio Guterres, UN Secretary General
a6971.name: Antonio Guterres
a6971.title: UN Secretary General
a6971.speech: Condemned Moscow's "veiled threats" to use nuclear weapons, saying such threats "have spiked nuclear risks to levels not seen since the darkest days of the Cold War" ; "These threats are unacceptable."

a6971.speaker: UN General Assembly resolution
a6971.name: UN General Assembly resolution
a6971.speech: Demanded Moscow immediately and unconditionally withdraw from Ukraine, and reaffirmed support for Ukraine's "sovereignty" and "territorial integrity," rejecting any Russian claims to the parts of the country it occupies.

a7003.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a7003.name: Marco Rubio
a7003.title: US Secretary of State
a7003.speech: Announced that the vast majority of USAID's programmes have been terminated after a six-week purge. On X, Rubio said that the initiatives "spent tens of billions in ways that did not serve" or harmed US interests ; said that after the review, the US was "officially ending" about 5,200 of USAID's 6,200 programmes ; "In consultation with Congress, we intend for the remaining 18% of programmes we are keeping....to be administered more effectively under the State Department" ; thanked Doge and State Department staff "who worked very long hours to achieve this overdue and historic reform."

a7003.speaker: Humanitarian organisations around the world
a7003.name: Humanitarian organisations around the world
a7003.speech: Have warned that the controversial move to end long-running US aid programmes is already having dire consequences around the world, potentially endangering lives.

a7003.speaker: The Trump administration
a7003.name: The Trump administration
a7003.speech: Has repeatedly made clear that it wants overseas spending to be closely aligned with its "America First" approach.

a7003.speaker: Democrats and various humanitarian organisations
a7003.name: Democrats and various humanitarian organisations
a7003.speech: Have characterised the shutdown of USAID's programmes – which were funded by Congress – as illegal, prompting several lawsuits.

a7105.speaker: High Court three-judge panel led by Judge Ndunguru (ruling)
a7105.name: High Court three-judge panel led by Judge Ndunguru (ruling)
a7105.speech: Dismissed Tundu Lissu's preliminary objections challenging the court's jurisdiction; ruled that it had jurisdiction to hear the case despite alleged procedural flaws at the committal stage ; also dismissed Lissu's claims that repeated adjournments at the lower court without stated reasons, the concealment of witnesses, and the denial of proper documentation had violated his rights.

a7105.speaker: Tundu Lissu, Tanzanian opposition leader
a7105.name: Tundu Lissu
a7105.title: Tanzanian opposition leader
a7105.speech: Argued against the very nature of the charges in a dramatic courtroom session.

a7105.speaker: Nassoro Katuga, state attorney
a7105.name: Nassoro Katuga
a7105.title: state attorney
a7105.speech: Indicated the prosecution was ready to proceed with reading the charges but immediately requested an adjournment to allow more preparation time.

a7105.speaker: Tanzania Police Force (statement, September 15, 2025)
a7105.name: Tanzania Police Force (statement
a7105.title: September 15, 2025)
a7105.speech: Said some of Polepole's allegations are criminal in nature and require evidence: "The Tanzania Police Force would like to inform the public that it opened an investigation file and has continued investigating various allegations made by Humphrey Herson Polepole since July 2025," ; "The allegations he has made, and continues to make, as he has described them, indicate the presence of criminal offenses and, according to the law, require evidence to substantiate them when they are presented in court," ; "In addition to gathering evidence, the Police Force has been making efforts to find him so that he can provide a statement/evidence. Therefore, through this statement, the Police Force continues to direct him to report to the Office of the Director of Criminal Investigations so that he can provide a statement/evidence."

a7105.speaker: Bank of Tanzania, Statement of Financial Position for August 2025
a7105.name: Bank of Tanzania
a7105.title: Statement of Financial Position for August 2025
a7105.speech: Shows that the Bank has strengthened its gold reserves, reaching gold worth 821.8 billion shillings as of August 31, 2025.

a7105.speaker: Bank of Tanzania, July 2025 Monetary Policy Report
a7105.name: Bank of Tanzania
a7105.title: July 2025 Monetary Policy Report
a7105.speech: Explained that gold purchases were aimed at strengthening the shilling amid global challenges: "The escalating geopolitical tensions, trade frictions, and changes in U.S. foreign aid policies added to global uncertainty, prompting banks to rebalance their portfolios and manage risk exposure," ; "Domestic gold purchases by the Bank have increased liquidity, which has partly reduced pressure on the shilling."

a7105.speaker: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of Tanzania
a7105.name: Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) of Tanzania
a7105.speech: Announced on Monday that it had upheld an objection filed by the Attorney General, ruling that Luhaga Mpina lacks the qualifications to contest the presidency because he has not been properly sponsored by a political party ; cited provisions of the Elections Act and accompanying regulations in its decision to remove Mpina from the presidential candidates list.

a7105.speaker: Attorney General of Tanzania
a7105.name: Attorney General of Tanzania
a7105.speech: Argued that Mpina's nomination by ACT Wazalendo violated the party's internal procedures, effectively meaning he lacks proper political party sponsorship required under Tanzanian law.

a7105.speaker: Witnesses (Kawe market fire)
a7105.name: Witnesses (Kawe market fire)
a7105.speech: Reported that the fire broke out at around 11:00 p.m. on Sunday, September 14, 2025.

a7105.speaker: Albert Chalamila, Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a7105.name: Albert Chalamila
a7105.title: Dar es Salaam Regional Commissioner
a7105.speech: Pledged Tsh 100 million to support traders whose businesses were destroyed in the Kawe food market fire; directed the Regional Administrative Secretary to allocate Tsh 100 million, which will be distributed to the traders on September 16, 2025, after they have been properly organized and agree on how they will use the fund through their leadership.

a7129.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwean Minister of Women's Affairs and Small and Medium Enterprise Development
a7129.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a7129.title: Zimbabwean Minister of Women's Affairs and Small and Medium Enterprise Development
a7129.speech: Stressed that more than 70% of Zimbabwe's population lives in rural areas and depends on agriculture, insisting on the need for modern equipment such as tractors and combine harvesters to improve productivity: "We want to be your partners. More than 70% of Zimbabweans live in rural areas and till the land," she declared.

a7129.speaker: Monica Mutsvangwa, Zimbabwean Minister of Women's Affairs and Small and Medium Enterprise Development
a7129.name: Monica Mutsvangwa
a7129.title: Zimbabwean Minister of Women's Affairs and Small and Medium Enterprise Development
a7129.speech: Also expressed keen interest in Belarusian dairy products, praising their quality and affirming Zimbabwe's willingness to import them; in exchange, Harare is offering to export seasonal fruit, particularly those not available in Belarus during the winter.

a7152.speaker: Nail Olpak, President of the Foreign Economic Relations Board (DEİK)
a7152.name: Nail Olpak
a7152.title: President of the Foreign Economic Relations Board (DEİK)
a7152.speech: “TABEF 2025 will be a strategic platform for deepening economic partnerships and consolidating the vision of mutual development between Türkiye and Africa,” he stressed, underlining the role of Turkish economic diplomacy in diversifying international trade.

a7152.speaker: DEİK (Foreign Economic Relations Board) data
a7152.name: DEİK (Foreign Economic Relations Board) data
a7152.speech: According to DEİK data, bilateral trade between Turkey and Africa surpassed 45 billion dollars in 2024.

a7152.speaker: Emine Erdoğan, First Lady of the Republic of Turkey
a7152.name: Emine Erdoğan
a7152.title: First Lady of the Republic of Turkey
a7152.speech: “Women play a central role in the economic and social transformation of Africa and Turkey. This dialogue is an opportunity to promote equality and women's entrepreneurship,” she said in a note from the organisers.

a7152.speaker: DEİK (Foreign Economic Relations Board)
a7152.name: DEİK (Foreign Economic Relations Board)
a7152.speech: States that the forum will be “a catalyst for transformative projects,” with an emphasis on public-private partnerships and the integration of regional value chains.

a7152.speaker: Fuat Tosyalı, coordinating president of the Türkiye-Africa Business Councils
a7152.name: Fuat Tosyalı
a7152.title: coordinating president of the Türkiye-Africa Business Councils
a7152.speech: “We believe that Türkiye-Africa economic cooperation can be an engine of shared prosperity, creating jobs, innovation and sustainable solutions,” he reinforced.

a7173.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.name: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.speech: Expresses deep concern about the implications of the immediate funding pause for HIV programmes in low- and middle-income countries. These programmes provide access to life-saving HIV therapy to more than 30 million people worldwide. Globally, 39.9 million people were living with HIV at the end of 2023. A funding halt for HIV programmes can put people living with HIV at immediate increased risk of illness and death and undermine efforts to prevent transmission in communities and countries. Such measures, if prolonged, could lead to rises in new infections and deaths, reversing decades of progress and potentially taking the world back to the 1980s and 1990s when millions died of HIV every year globally, including many in the United States of America. ; For the global community, this could result in significant setbacks to progress in partnerships and investments in scientific advances that have been the cornerstone of good public health programming, including innovative diagnostics, affordable medicines, and community delivery models of HIV care.

a7173.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.name: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.speech: “We call on the United States Government to enable additional exemptions to ensure the delivery of lifesaving HIV treatment and care.”

a7173.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.name: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.speech: Said the current funding pause for PEPFAR will have a direct impact on millions of lives that depend on the predictable supply of safe and effective antiretroviral treatment; that PEPFAR works in over 50 countries, has saved more than 26 million lives over two decades and is currently providing HIV treatment for more than 20 million people living with HIV globally, including 566 000 children under 15 years of age; and that a sudden and prolonged stop to programmes does not allow for a managed transition and puts the lives of millions at risk, since PEPFAR and partners, including WHO, have been working on sustainability plans with countries for greater country ownership and reduced donor support up to and beyond 2030.

a7173.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.name: World Health Organization (WHO) statement
a7173.speech: Said WHO is committed to support PEPFAR and other partners, as well as national governments, in managing change processes effectively to minimize the impact on people living with HIV.

a7344.speaker: Botswana Medical Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) (statement)
a7344.name: Botswana Medical Regulatory Authority (BoMRA) (statement)
a7344.speech: Has reassured the public that recently imported medical products from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) were not compromised after brief exposure to sunlight during a ceremony at Sir Seretse Khama International Airport; emphasized in a statement that all due processes and safety measures were followed to protect the integrity and quality of the products, maintained that the medicines were handled according to international standards and dismissed claims that the temporary exposure posed any risk. ; Said it has been coordinating closely with the Ministry of Health and international bodies since the declaration of a public health emergency by President Duma Boko to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements for emergency medical imports.

a7344.speaker: Botswana Medical Regulatory Authority (BoMRA)
a7344.name: Botswana Medical Regulatory Authority (BoMRA)
a7344.speech: Noted that all medical products entering Botswana undergo rigorous vetting, including documentation reviews, pre-shipment inspections, and testing where necessary, and that once in the country they are further monitored through pharmacovigilance and surveillance programs; confirmed that the Dubai shipment was subject to the same stringent procedures and reaffirmed its commitment to consistently applying regulatory standards to safeguard public health.

a7344.speaker: Peter Baleseng, president of the Botswana Nurses Union (BONU)
a7344.name: Peter Baleseng
a7344.title: president of the Botswana Nurses Union (BONU)
a7344.speech: Said he was not fully briefed on the incident but stressed that medicines, particularly vaccines, should not be exposed to direct sunlight; noted that even small shipments are usually transported in specialized containers. "The public cannot just be mad for nothing; the outburst shows that something was done wrong in terms of handling the medicines," Baleseng said. He also questioned the need for a celebratory event to mark the drug procurement, describing such displays as unnecessary for government operations.

a7436.speaker: Egeland, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.name: Egeland
a7436.title: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.speech: "I am truly shocked by the conditions I have seen in and around the city of Goma. The lives of hundreds of thousands of people here in eastern DRC are hanging by a thread." ; "Right across North and South Kivu, people have been repeatedly compelled to flee camps, where essential facilities were often already inadequate. Now, most find themselves in locations that lack shelter, basic sanitation, or drinking water, with diseases such as cholera rapidly increasing as a result." ; "Our courageous staff remained in Goma during the height of the conflict, and were supporting the community once again within just a few days. But many displaced people I've listened to this week have lost everything after years of violence. It is unacceptable that a small number of humanitarian organisations are faced with a vast mountain of needs. It is high time that assistance here matches the vast scale of human suffering. Long term solutions must be enabled, with children quickly allowed to return to school, banks to re-open, and an immediate end to violence and threats of violence against civilians."

a7436.speaker: Egeland, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.name: Egeland
a7436.title: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.speech: "Fighting and conflict are still continuing, with thousands of families caught in limbo, without the means to rebuild or cultivate food. The situation facing civilians in eastern DRC has for years been a stain on the international community: now it has become even worse."

a7436.speaker: Egeland, Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.name: Egeland
a7436.title: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC)
a7436.speech: "The level of global neglect experienced by civilians in eastern DRC should shame world leaders. Now, at a point of deep insecurity and with many families having returned to their areas of origin, there must be concerted action to finally support the population properly. Humanitarian and development assistance must now take priority: the people of DRC must not be faced with simply more of the same."

a7436.speaker: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a7436.name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
a7436.speech: In North Kivu and South Kivu provinces, 1,157,090 people have been displaced since the start of 2025, and 1,787,298 have returned to their areas of origin; between January and February 2025, over 660,000 people were displaced out of temporary collective sites in Goma and on the outskirts of Nyiragongo territory; across DRC, almost seven million people are internally displaced, with almost 90 per cent displaced due to conflict.

a7436.speaker: NRC survey (conducted February 14-17, covering 138 households)
a7436.name: NRC survey (conducted February 14-17
a7436.title: covering 138 households)
a7436.speech: In villages around Shasha, west of Goma, over 90 per cent of people lack proper latrines or washing facilities, and drinking water connections have been destroyed.

a7436.speaker: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report on the ten most neglected displacement crises
a7436.name: Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) report on the ten most neglected displacement crises
a7436.speech: DRC has featured every year since the inception of the report, including thrice as the most neglected crisis and four times as the second.

a7436.speaker: UNHCR / UNHRC and 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan
a7436.name: UNHCR / UNHRC and 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan
a7436.speech: The Humanitarian Response Plan for DRC regularly receives less than half of what is required to meet basic humanitarian needs. In 2023 it was 41 per cent funded; in 2024 it was 44 per cent funded. In 2025, the humanitarian community in the DRC calls for $2.54 billion to provide lifesaving assistance to 11 million people affected by crises.

a7436.speaker: UN OCHA
a7436.name: UN OCHA
a7436.speech: In 2024 the United States provided over two-thirds of the supplied funding for the DRC humanitarian response plan.

a7436.speaker: DRC Education Cluster
a7436.name: DRC Education Cluster
a7436.speech: In North and South Kivu provinces, 5,927 schools remain closed resulting in almost 2,000,000 children with no access to education.

a7436.speaker: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)
a7436.name: Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)
a7436.speech: Food security remains a major concern across DRC, which is currently the largest hunger crisis in the world, with 27.7m people experiencing high acute food insecurity.

a7521.speaker: Organisers of the protest (coalition of civil society organizations and concerned citizens)
a7521.name: Organisers of the protest (coalition of civil society organizations and concerned citizens)
a7521.speech: Outlined several major grievances against the Tonse Alliance government, which they believe has failed to address the nation's critical challenges: the collapse of the Affordable Inputs Program (AIP) and rising cost of fertilizer; the persistent lack of foreign exchange reserves; accusations that government officials enabled widespread corruption; criticism of the Malawi Electoral Commission (MEC) and National Registration Bureau (NRB) for alleged inefficiencies and partisan behaviour; and the claim that the MCP-led administration has failed to fulfil its promises, with inflation and unemployment surging. ; Outlined specific demands: the impeachment of President Chakwera, immediate reforms within MEC and NRB, agricultural policies ensuring affordable fertilizer and access to food, and robust interventions to address the forex crisis, stabilize the economy and combat rising inflation. ; Are rallying all Malawians to join the demonstration, emphasizing that the event transcends political divisions and focuses on securing a better future for the nation.

a7521.speaker: Protest organizer (anonymous)
a7521.name: Protest organizer (anonymous)
a7521.speech: "Malawi is at a crossroads. This is about ensuring accountability and safeguarding the rights of every citizen. We must act now to build the country we want."

a7521.speaker: Government of Malawi (non-response)
a7521.name: Government of Malawi (non-response)
a7521.speech: So far, the government has not officially commented on the planned protests.

a7521.speaker: Analysts
a7521.name: Analysts
a7521.speech: Believe that officials may attempt to dismiss the demonstrations as politically motivated, but the rising dissatisfaction among citizens suggests deeper discontent with the administration.

a7521.speaker: A Lilongwe resident
a7521.name: A Lilongwe resident
a7521.speech: "It's time we voiced our frustrations. These protests are not just about politics; they're about survival."
